eras.name: Creation and the first families
eras.summary: The world made and called good, the first people placed in it, and the first fracture — disobedience, exile from the garden, and a brother's murder.

eras.name: The Flood
eras.summary: A world grown violent, one righteous family preserved through it, and a covenant never to unmake the earth by water again.

eras.name: The Patriarchs
eras.summary: Four generations — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph — through whom God begins to build a nation out of one childless couple's promise.

eras.name: The Exodus
eras.summary: Israel is enslaved in Egypt, delivered through the plagues and the Red Sea, receives the law at Sinai, and spends forty years in the wilderness before arriving at the plains of Moab, ready to cross into the promised land.
eras.approxRange: roughly 40 years, from slavery in Egypt to the plains of Moab

eras.name: The Conquest of Canaan
eras.summary: Under Joshua, Israel crosses the Jordan into the promised land and takes it city by city — some through overwhelming victory, one through failure and correction, one through being deceived.
eras.approxRange: immediately after the wilderness years, before the judges

eras.name: The Judges
eras.summary: A repeating cycle: Israel abandons Yahweh, is oppressed by a neighboring power, cries out, and God raises up a judge to deliver them — Ehud, Deborah, Gideon, Jephthah, Samson, and others — until the next cycle begins. Ruth’s quiet story of loyalty happens inside this same chaotic period, and ends by naming David’s great-grandparents.
eras.approxRange: centuries after the Exodus, before Israel's kings

eras.name: The United Kingdom
eras.summary: Israel’s first three kings reign over a unified nation: Saul, chosen and then rejected; David, the shepherd who becomes king and is promised an everlasting throne; and later Solomon, whose wisdom and excess both become legendary.
eras.approxRange: Israel’s first kings, before the kingdom splits

eras.name: The Divided Kingdom
eras.summary: After Solomon's death the kingdom splits in two: Rehoboam keeps Judah in the south, Jeroboam leads the ten northern tribes as Israel and sets up rival worship to keep them from Jerusalem. In the north, king Ahab marries Jezebel and promotes Baal worship, and the prophet Elijah confronts them both.
eras.approxRange: Israel splits into two kingdoms; the prophet Elijah's ministry in the north

eras.name: The Exile
eras.summary: Jerusalem falls to Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. The temple Solomon built is burned, the last king of Judah is blinded and dragged away in chains, and the people are carried into captivity — the end of the monarchy and the start of seventy years in a foreign land.
eras.approxRange: Judah carried into captivity in Babylon

eras.name: The Return from Exile
eras.summary: Cyrus of Persia's decree lets the exiles go home. Zerubbabel and Jeshua rebuild the altar and temple against fierce local opposition; a generation later Ezra brings the law back to the center of the people's life, and Nehemiah leaves the king's palace to rebuild Jerusalem's broken walls and enforce what the law demands.
eras.approxRange: The return to Judah and rebuilding of Jerusalem under Persian rule

eras.name: Esther and the Persian Diaspora
eras.summary: Not every exile returned. In the Persian capital of Susa, decades after the first return to Jerusalem, a Jewish orphan named Esther becomes queen, and when a powerful official plots to annihilate her people empire-wide, her hidden identity and a cousin's courage become Israel's only defense — with God's name never once mentioned, but his hand unmistakable throughout.
eras.approxRange: The Jews who remained in the Persian empire, under King Ahasuerus

eras.name: Job's Testing
eras.summary: Outside Israel's own history entirely — a blameless man in the land of Uz loses everything in a single day, then spends the rest of the book arguing honestly with God and three friends who insist his suffering must be deserved, until Yahweh himself answers him out of a whirlwind.
eras.approxRange: Undated, traditionally reckoned among the oldest stories in the Bible

eras.name: The Birth of Jesus
eras.summary: Gabriel announces two impossible births -- John to the aged priest Zacharias and Elizabeth, then Jesus to a virgin named Mary. Jesus is born in Bethlehem to a census-displaced family, worshiped by shepherds and, later, foreign astrologers, and hunted by a jealous king before his family flees to Egypt and settles in Nazareth.
eras.approxRange: The births of John the Baptist and Jesus, under Herod the Great

eras.name: Jesus's Ministry
eras.summary: For roughly three years, Jesus teaches, heals, and calls people to follow him across Galilee and Judea -- announcing the kingdom of God through parables, confronting religious leaders, performing miracles that reveal who he is, and gathering twelve disciples to carry the message forward.
eras.approxRange: Jesus's public ministry, from his baptism to his final journey to Jerusalem

eras.name: The Passion and Resurrection
eras.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem to a crowd's shouts of praise, teaches and confronts religious leaders in the temple all week, shares a final meal with his disciples, is betrayed, arrested, tried, and crucified -- then rises from the dead on the third day, appearing to his followers before ascending to heaven.
eras.approxRange: Jesus's final week in Jerusalem, through his resurrection and ascension

eras.name: The Early Church
eras.summary: Filled with the Holy Spirit at Pentecost, the apostles proclaim the risen Jesus in Jerusalem and beyond, performing signs, sharing everything in common, and facing growing opposition -- while the gospel spreads from a persecuted Jewish sect into a movement reaching Samaritans, Gentiles, and eventually Rome itself.
eras.approxRange: From Pentecost through the spread of the church across the Roman world

stories.title: The world is made
stories.summary: God speaks the heavens and the earth into being, fills them, makes humanity in his own image, and calls all of it very good.

stories.title: The garden
stories.summary: God forms the man from dust, breathes life into him, plants a garden for him to tend, and makes the woman so he is not alone.

stories.title: The fall
stories.summary: The serpent persuades the woman that God is holding out on her. She eats, gives to her husband, and the two of them are put out of the garden.

stories.title: Cain and Abel
stories.summary: God accepts Abel's offering and not Cain's. Warned that sin is crouching at his door, Cain kills his brother in the field anyway.

stories.title: The flood
stories.summary: In a violent generation Noah is found righteous. He builds the ark exactly as commanded, rides out the flood, and comes out to a rainbow and a promise.

stories.title: The call of Abram
stories.summary: God tells a seventy-five-year-old man to leave his country, his relatives and his father's house for a land he will only be shown once he goes. He goes.

stories.title: Abram and Lot part ways
stories.summary: Their herds outgrow the land. Abram, the elder, gives his nephew first choice; Lot takes the well-watered Jordan valley and settles toward Sodom.

stories.title: The covenant of the pieces
stories.summary: God promises Abram offspring as countless as the stars. Abram believes him, and it is credited to him as righteousness.

stories.title: Hagar and Ishmael
stories.summary: Tired of waiting, Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram. Hagar conceives, is mistreated, and flees — and meets the God who sees her.

stories.title: A new name, a new sign
stories.summary: God appears to ninety-nine-year-old Abram, renames him Abraham — father of many nations — and gives circumcision as the sign of an everlasting covenant.

stories.title: Three visitors and Sarah's laugh
stories.summary: Three strangers accept Abraham's hospitality and promise Sarah a son within the year. Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughs.

stories.title: Abraham pleads for Sodom
stories.summary: Abraham bargains with God for the city — down from fifty righteous to ten — appealing to the Judge of all the earth to do right.

stories.title: Isaac is born
stories.summary: At a hundred years old Abraham holds the son he was promised a quarter-century earlier. They name him Isaac — laughter.

stories.title: Hagar sent away
stories.summary: Sarah demands Hagar and Ishmael be sent off. Their water runs out in the wilderness; God hears the boy crying and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.

stories.title: The binding of Isaac
stories.summary: God asks Abraham for the son he waited a lifetime for. Abraham goes, knife raised — and God provides a ram caught in the thicket instead.

stories.title: Sarah is buried
stories.summary: Sarah dies at a hundred and twenty-seven. Abraham mourns her, then buys the cave of Machpelah — the first piece of the promised land he ever owns.

stories.title: Rebekah at the well
stories.summary: Abraham's servant asks God for a sign and Rebekah gives it — watering ten camels for a stranger. She agrees to go, and becomes Isaac's wife.

stories.title: Twins at war in the womb
stories.summary: Rebekah is barren twenty years, then carries twins who struggle inside her. Esau is born first; Jacob follows, gripping his heel.

stories.title: A birthright for a bowl of stew
stories.summary: Esau comes in from the field starving and trades his birthright as firstborn to Jacob for a meal.

stories.title: The stolen blessing
stories.summary: Rebekah dresses Jacob in Esau's clothes and goatskins. Blind Isaac blesses the wrong son, and Jacob has to run for his life.

stories.title: The ladder at Bethel
stories.summary: Fleeing with nothing but a staff, Jacob sleeps on a stone and dreams of a stairway to heaven. God stands above it and promises to keep him wherever he goes.

stories.title: Seven years for Rachel
stories.summary: Jacob the deceiver is deceived: he works seven years for Rachel and is given Leah instead, then works seven more. Leah bears sons; Rachel does not.

stories.title: Wrestling until daybreak
stories.summary: Alone at the Jabbok the night before facing Esau, Jacob wrestles a man until dawn, refuses to let go without a blessing, and limps away renamed Israel.

stories.title: Esau runs to meet him
stories.summary: Jacob braces for the brother he cheated, sending gifts ahead. Esau runs to him, embraces him, and weeps.

stories.title: Joseph's dreams
stories.summary: Jacob's favourite son tells his brothers he dreamed they would bow to him. They already hated him; now they cannot speak a kind word to him.

stories.title: Sold by his brothers
stories.summary: They see him coming and plot to kill him, throw him in a pit instead, and sell him to passing traders for twenty pieces of silver.

stories.title: Potiphar's house and prison
stories.summary: Yahweh is with Joseph and he prospers, until he refuses his master's wife and is thrown into prison for it.

stories.title: Dreams in prison and palace
stories.summary: Joseph interprets a cupbearer's and a baker's dreams, is forgotten for two years, then reads Pharaoh's dream of famine and is made second in Egypt.

stories.title: "I am Joseph"
stories.summary: After testing the brothers who sold him, Joseph sends everyone out and weeps aloud: God sent him ahead of them to preserve life.

stories.title: Jacob comes to Egypt
stories.summary: Told his son is alive, Jacob goes down to Egypt to see him, and the family settles in Goshen through the famine.

stories.title: Jacob blesses his sons
stories.summary: Dying, Jacob gathers his twelve sons and speaks over each one what they will become — the shape of the tribes of Israel.

stories.title: "You meant evil; God meant it for good"
stories.summary: With their father dead, the brothers fear revenge. Joseph weeps and tells them what he has understood all along about the God who redirected their evil.

stories.title: Hidden, then found
stories.summary: To save her infant son from Pharaoh's death decree, Jochebed hides him three months, then sets him afloat in a basket on the Nile - where Pharaoh's own daughter finds and raises him.

stories.title: Moses flees to Midian
stories.summary: After killing an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, Moses flees for his life, settles in Midian, defends a priest's daughters at a well, and marries one of them.

stories.title: The burning bush
stories.summary: Keeping his father-in-law's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush that burns without being consumed. God calls him by name, reveals his own name, and sends him back to Egypt to deliver Israel - over every objection Moses raises.

stories.title: Aaron meets him in the wilderness
stories.summary: Moses takes his wife and sons and returns to Egypt. Aaron goes out to meet him at God's mountain and kisses him; together they gather Israel's elders, and the people believe and bow down to worship.

stories.title: "Let my people go"
stories.summary: Moses and Aaron confront Pharaoh again and again with the same demand. Each time he refuses, a plague strikes Egypt; each time it lifts, his heart hardens again.

stories.title: The Passover
stories.summary: On the night of the tenth plague, Israel is told to mark their doorposts with blood so death will pass over them. That night Egypt's firstborn die, and Pharaoh finally lets Israel go.

stories.title: Crossing the Red Sea
stories.summary: With Pharaoh's army closing in and the sea ahead, Moses tells the people to stand still. The sea divides, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the pursuing army is destroyed.

stories.title: The song of the sea
stories.summary: On the far shore, Moses sings of what Yahweh has done. Miriam takes up a tambourine, and all the women dance and sing after her.

stories.title: Bread from heaven, water from the rock
stories.summary: In the wilderness the people run out of food, then water. God answers both times — bread appearing with the dew each morning, water from a struck rock.

stories.title: The battle with Amalek
stories.summary: Joshua leads Israel's fighting men against Amalek while Moses holds up his hands on a hilltop. When his hands grow heavy, Aaron and another man hold them up until sunset, and Joshua wins.

stories.title: The covenant at Sinai
stories.summary: At the mountain, God offers Israel a covenant — his own possession, a kingdom of priests — and gives the commandments, beginning with no other gods and honoring father and mother.

stories.title: The golden calf
stories.summary: While Moses is on the mountain, the people grow impatient and ask Aaron to make them a god. Moses comes down, breaks the tablets in anger, and then goes back up to beg God to forgive them rather than destroy them. Joshua, meanwhile, has not left the tent.

stories.title: "Merciful and gracious"
stories.summary: God gives Moses new tablets and passes before him, proclaiming his own character: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abundant in loving kindness — and still just.

stories.title: The glory fills the tabernacle
stories.summary: The tabernacle is finished exactly as instructed. A cloud covers it, and Yahweh's glory fills it so completely that even Moses cannot enter.

stories.title: Aaron ordained as priest
stories.summary: After seven days of ordination rites, Aaron and his sons offer the first sacrifices as priests. Fire comes out from before Yahweh and consumes the offering, and the whole camp shouts and falls on its face.

stories.title: Nadab and Abihu
stories.summary: Two of Aaron's sons offer incense with fire God never authorized, and fire from Yahweh kills them on the spot, in front of their father. Moses tells Aaron this is exactly what God meant by being shown holy among those who come near him. Aaron says nothing.

stories.title: The blasphemer
stories.summary: A man in the camp curses Yahweh's name during a fight. Israel holds him in custody until Yahweh tells Moses exactly what to do: everyone who heard him lays a hand on his head, and the whole community stones him.

stories.title: Miriam and Aaron oppose Moses
stories.summary: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses over his Cushite wife, and challenge whether Yahweh speaks only through him. Miriam is struck with leprosy; Moses immediately begs God to heal her, and she is shut outside the camp seven days.

stories.title: The twelve spies
stories.summary: Twelve men scout Canaan. Ten report giants and fortified cities and spread fear; Caleb and Joshua insist God will give them the land. The people side with the fearful report and refuse to go up, so God condemns that whole generation to wander forty years and die in the wilderness — only Caleb and Joshua will enter.

stories.title: Korah's rebellion
stories.summary: Korah and his followers accuse Moses and Aaron of taking too much power for themselves. Moses says the ground itself will show who Yahweh sent — and the earth opens and swallows Korah, his household, and everything he owns.

stories.title: Water from the rock, again
stories.summary: Nearly forty years after the first time, the people again have no water. This time God tells Moses to speak to the rock — but Moses, furious, strikes it twice instead. The water still comes, but Moses and Aaron are told neither of them will enter the promised land because of it.

stories.title: Miriam and Aaron die
stories.summary: Miriam dies at Kadesh. Later that year, Moses strips Aaron of his priestly garments on Mount Hor and puts them on his son Eleazar; Aaron dies there, and all Israel mourns him thirty days.

stories.title: The bronze serpent
stories.summary: The people complain again about the journey, and Yahweh sends venomous snakes among them. When they confess and ask Moses to intercede, God tells him to make a bronze snake and put it on a pole — anyone who is bitten and looks at it lives.

stories.title: Balaam's donkey
stories.summary: Hired by a foreign king to curse Israel, the prophet Balaam is stopped on the road by his own donkey, who sees the angel of Yahweh blocking the way and speaks in protest. Balaam's eyes are opened too — and when the moment comes, he blesses Israel instead of cursing them, seeing a king who will rise from Jacob far in the future.

stories.title: Moses commissions Joshua
stories.summary: In front of all Israel, Moses tells Joshua to be strong and courageous — he will lead the people into the land Yahweh swore to their fathers. Moses lays his hands on him, and Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom.

stories.title: Moses views the land, and dies
stories.summary: From Mount Nebo, Yahweh shows Moses the whole land he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and tells him he will not cross over into it himself. Moses dies there at a hundred twenty, his eye undimmed and his strength unspent, and no prophet like him has risen in Israel since.

stories.title: Joshua takes charge
stories.summary: As Moses' successor, Joshua hears God's charge directly: be strong and courageous, keep the law always on his lips, and know that God is with him exactly as he was with Moses.

stories.title: Rahab and the spies
stories.summary: Joshua sends two spies into Jericho, where a woman named Rahab hides them from the king's men on her roof. She tells them Jericho is already terrified of Israel, and asks only that her family be spared when the city falls. They agree, and she lowers them from the wall by a rope, marking her window with a scarlet cord.

stories.title: Crossing the Jordan
stories.summary: The priests carry the ark into the flooding Jordan, and the water stops flowing the moment their feet touch it. All Israel crosses on dry ground, and twelve stones are set up as a memorial.

stories.title: The fall of Jericho
stories.summary: For six days Israel marches silently around Jericho once a day; on the seventh, they march around it seven times, then shout at the priests' trumpet blast — and the wall falls flat. Rahab and her family are the only ones spared.

stories.title: Achan's sin, and the second battle for Ai
stories.summary: Israel is unexpectedly routed at Ai. Joshua learns why: Achan secretly kept plunder from Jericho that had been devoted to destruction. Once Achan is exposed and stoned, Israel attacks Ai again and takes it.

stories.title: The Gibeonite deception
stories.summary: Hearing what happened to Jericho and Ai, the Gibeonites disguise themselves as travelers from a distant country and trick Israel's leaders into a treaty of peace, without anyone asking God first.

stories.title: The sun stands still
stories.summary: Defending the Gibeonites he had just made a treaty with, Joshua asks Yahweh, in front of all Israel, to make the sun and moon stand still — and they do, for a day with no equal before or since, while Israel finishes the battle.

stories.title: Caleb receives Hebron
stories.summary: Forty-five years after he first believed Israel could take the land, eighty-five-year-old Caleb asks Joshua to keep the promise: give him the hill country of the very Anakim that once made the other ten spies afraid.

stories.title: "As for me and my house"
stories.summary: Old and near death, Joshua gathers Israel and reminds them everything Yahweh promised has come true. He tells them to choose today whom they will serve — and commits himself and his household to Yahweh, whatever they decide.

stories.title: Ehud and Eglon
stories.summary: Israel's tribute-bearer to Moab's king is secretly a left-handed assassin. Ehud gets Eglon alone with a message from God, and delivers it with a hidden sword instead of words. Israel then defeats Moab and gets eighty years of peace.

stories.title: Deborah, Barak, and Jael
stories.summary: Deborah the prophetess summons Barak to fight the army oppressing Israel; he refuses to go without her, so she agrees but tells him the real victory will belong to a woman instead of him. Barak routs the army, and its fleeing commander Sisera is killed in his sleep by Jael, a tent peg through his temple.

stories.title: Gideon and the three hundred
stories.summary: Gideon is found threshing wheat in a wine press, hiding it from raiders, when an angel calls him a mighty man of valor. He tests God twice with a fleece before believing it, then watches his army shrink from thirty-two thousand to three hundred men — so that when Midian is routed with nothing but trumpets, torches, and jars, no one can say Israel saved itself.

stories.title: Jephthah's vow
stories.summary: An outcast who became Israel's military leader, Jephthah vows that if God gives him victory over Ammon, he will sacrifice whatever comes out of his house first to meet him. He wins — and his only child, his daughter, comes out dancing to celebrate. He keeps the vow.

stories.title: Samson's birth
stories.summary: An angel tells a childless woman she will bear a son set apart to God from birth, who will begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. She names him Samson.

stories.title: Samson and Delilah
stories.summary: Samson falls in love with Delilah, who is paid to discover the secret of his strength. She wears him down until he tells her the truth — that he is a Nazirite from birth — and has his hair cut while he sleeps. Blinded and enslaved, he prays for strength one last time and pulls down the temple of Dagon on everyone in it, himself included.

stories.title: Famine drives them to Moab
stories.summary: A famine sends Elimelech, Naomi, and their two sons from Bethlehem to Moab. The sons marry Moabite women, Ruth and Orpah. Then all three men die, leaving Naomi with her daughters-in-law and nothing else.

stories.title: "Where you go, I will go"
stories.summary: Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to go home to Moab and remarry. Orpah, weeping, does. Ruth refuses to leave, binding herself to Naomi's people and Naomi's God. They arrive in Bethlehem with nothing, at the start of the barley harvest.

stories.title: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field
stories.summary: Ruth goes out to gather leftover grain to feed herself and Naomi, and happens into the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's dead husband. He has noticed everything she has done for Naomi, and tells his workers to leave extra for her on purpose.

stories.title: Ruth asks for redemption
stories.summary: Naomi sends Ruth to Boaz at the threshing floor at night to ask him, as a near kinsman, to spread his garment over her — a claim of protection and marriage, not scandal. Boaz agrees, but names a closer relative who has first right to redeem her.

stories.title: Boaz redeems Ruth
stories.summary: At the town gate, the nearer kinsman declines to redeem Elimelech's field once he learns it comes with Ruth. Boaz redeems it himself and marries her. She bears a son, Obed — the grandfather of Jesse, the father of David.

stories.title: Hannah's prayer
stories.summary: Barren and taunted for it, Hannah vows that if God gives her a son she will give him back to serve at the tabernacle for life. She bears Samuel, and when he is weaned, brings him to the priest Eli and keeps her vow — then sings a song of praise instead of grief.

stories.title: Samuel's call, and the fall of Eli's house
stories.summary: A boy still serving in the tabernacle, Samuel hears Yahweh call his name at night and mistakes it for Eli three times before Eli realizes what's happening and tells him how to answer. Not long after, the Philistines capture the ark in battle and kill Eli's sons; when the old priest hears the ark is gone, he falls backward and dies.

stories.title: Israel demands a king
stories.summary: Old and watching his sons fail as judges, Samuel is asked by the elders for a king like the other nations. God tells him the people haven't rejected Samuel — they've rejected God. Samuel anoints Saul in private, then presents him to the people, who shout, "Long live the king!"

stories.title: Saul's rejection
stories.summary: Saul offers a sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel, and later spares the Amalekite king and the best of the plunder against a direct command. Samuel tells him plainly: to obey is better than sacrifice, and because he has rejected Yahweh's word, Yahweh has rejected him as king.

stories.title: David anointed
stories.summary: Sent to Jesse's house in Bethlehem, Samuel is ready to anoint the tallest, most impressive brother — until God tells him not to judge by appearance, because he looks at the heart. The youngest, still out with the sheep, is the one anointed.

stories.title: David and Goliath
stories.summary: While Saul's army cowers before a nine-foot Philistine champion, a shepherd boy who came to bring his brothers lunch volunteers to fight him — with no armor, a sling, and the conviction that the battle belongs to Yahweh, not to swords.

stories.title: David and Jonathan
stories.summary: Saul's son Jonathan loves David as his own soul, and the two make a covenant of loyalty that outlasts Saul's growing hatred — Jonathan even warns David when his father means to kill him, choosing the friendship over his own claim to the throne.

stories.title: Saul hunts David
stories.summary: Jealous of David's popularity, Saul tries to pin him to the wall with a spear, then hunts him through the wilderness for years. Twice David has a clear chance to kill him and refuses, unwilling to raise a hand against Yahweh's anointed king.

stories.title: The witch of Endor
stories.summary: With Yahweh silent and the Philistines closing in, Saul — who had banned mediums from the land — disguises himself and asks a medium to bring up Samuel's spirit. What he hears is his own death sentence for tomorrow.

stories.title: The death of Saul and Jonathan
stories.summary: Israel is routed on Mount Gilboa. Jonathan and his brothers are killed, and Saul, badly wounded and refusing capture, falls on his own sword.

stories.title: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan
stories.summary: News of Saul and Jonathan's deaths reaches David at Ziklag. Rather than relief at his rival's end, he tears his clothes and mourns, then composes a lament — grief for Saul as the anointed king, and for Jonathan a love "passing the love of women."

stories.title: David becomes king over all Israel
stories.summary: After years of civil war between Saul's house and David's, the elders of every tribe come to Hebron and anoint David king over a united Israel. He takes the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and makes it his city — Jerusalem.

stories.title: Michal despises David's worship
stories.summary: David brings the ark of the covenant up to Jerusalem, dancing before it with all his might in plain linen. Watching from a window, his wife Michal — Saul's daughter — despises him in her heart for humiliating himself in front of servant girls. She never bears a child.

stories.title: God's covenant with David
stories.summary: David wants to build God a house. Instead, through the prophet Nathan, God promises to build David a house — a dynasty and a throne established forever, a promise later generations would read as pointing toward the Messiah.

stories.title: David and Mephibosheth
stories.summary: Years after Jonathan's death, David asks if anyone from Saul's house is left so he can show them kindness for Jonathan's sake. He finds Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, crippled in both feet, and restores his grandfather's land and a permanent seat at the king's table.

stories.title: David and Bathsheba
stories.summary: While his army is at war, David stays behind, sees Bathsheba bathing, and sends for her, though he knows she is another man's wife. When she becomes pregnant, he tries to cover it up, and when that fails, arranges for her husband Uriah to die in battle.

stories.title: "You are the man"
stories.summary: Nathan tells David a story about a rich man who steals a poor man's only lamb, and watches David condemn the man in outrage — before telling him, "You are the man." David confesses on the spot; Nathan says his sin is forgiven, but its cost will follow him.

stories.title: Amnon and Tamar
stories.summary: David's firstborn son Amnon forces himself on his half-sister Tamar, then hates her afterward and throws her out in shame. Her full brother Absalom says nothing publicly but waits two years, then has his servants kill Amnon at a feast.

stories.title: Absalom's rebellion
stories.summary: Reconciled with his father after years of exile, Absalom sets himself up at the city gate, telling every petitioner he'd judge their case better than the king would — quietly stealing the loyalty of Israel. He then declares himself king at Hebron, and David flees Jerusalem rather than fight his own son in the city.

stories.title: The death of Absalom
stories.summary: Riding through the forest during the battle against his father's loyalists, Absalom's head catches in the branches of a great oak, leaving him hanging helpless. Against David's express order to deal gently with him, Joab kills him. When David hears, his victory turns to grief: "O Absalom, my son, my son!"

stories.title: The threshing floor of Ornan
stories.summary: David orders a census of Israel against advice, and a plague follows that kills seventy thousand. Seeing the angel of Yahweh at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, David buys the site at full price — refusing to offer God something that cost him nothing — and builds an altar there. Fire falls from heaven, and David declares this the place for the house of God.

stories.title: David prepares for the temple
stories.summary: Barred from building the temple himself because he was a man of war, David spends his last years gathering materials on a vast scale and charging his son Solomon with the work. "Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don't be afraid, for Yahweh God is with you; he will not fail you until all the work is finished."

stories.title: David's prayer of blessing
stories.summary: Before the whole assembly, having given his own treasure to the temple fund and seen the people give willingly too, David blesses Yahweh: "Yours, Yahweh, is the greatness, the power, the glory... all things come from you, and of your own we have given you."

stories.title: Solomon becomes king
stories.summary: With David old and dying, his son Adonijah declares himself king without his father's word. David instead has Solomon anointed and set on the throne, and Solomon secures his rule once his father dies.

stories.title: Solomon asks for wisdom
stories.summary: God appears to Solomon in a dream and tells him to ask for whatever he wants. Instead of riches or long life, Solomon asks for an understanding heart to govern well — and God gives him more wisdom than anyone before or after him.

stories.title: Solomon's judgment
stories.summary: Two women, each having lost a child, both claim the same living baby. Solomon orders the child cut in half — and the real mother instantly gives him up rather than see him killed, exposing which woman is telling the truth.

stories.title: Solomon builds the temple
stories.summary: Solomon builds a permanent house for God in Jerusalem. When it's finished and the ark is brought in, a cloud fills the temple with Yahweh's glory — and Solomon himself asks, in his dedication prayer, whether God could truly dwell in a house built by human hands. The Chronicles account adds fire falling from heaven at the dedication, and God's night-time answer to Solomon: if his people humble themselves, pray, and turn back, he will hear and heal their land.

stories.title: The queen of Sheba
stories.summary: Hearing of Solomon's fame, the queen of Sheba travels to test him with hard questions. After seeing his wisdom and his kingdom firsthand, she admits not even half of what she'd heard had been told her.

stories.title: Solomon's downfall
stories.summary: In his old age, Solomon's many foreign wives turn his heart after other gods, and his devotion to Yahweh is no longer whole like his father David's. God tells him the kingdom will be torn from his family — though not in his own lifetime, and not all of it.

stories.title: The kingdom divides
stories.summary: Solomon's son Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice to ease the people's burden, choosing instead the young men's counsel to rule even harder than his father. Ten tribes rebel on the spot and follow Jeroboam instead, splitting the kingdom into Israel and Judah.

stories.title: Abijah relies on Yahweh
stories.summary: Rehoboam's son Abijah faces Jeroboam's army, twice the size of his own and already flanking him. He calls across the lines that Judah has not forsaken Yahweh or his priests, and warns Israel not to fight against God. Judah wins because they relied on the God of their fathers.

stories.title: Jeroboam's golden calves
stories.summary: Afraid that worship trips to Jerusalem will win his new subjects back to Rehoboam, Jeroboam sets up two golden calves at Dan and Bethel and tells Israel these, not the temple, are their gods now.

stories.title: Asa's reliance, and his failure
stories.summary: Outnumbered by a vast Ethiopian army, king Asa prays that with Yahweh there is no difference between the mighty and the powerless, and Judah is delivered. A prophet tells him Yahweh is found by those who seek him. Years later, threatened again, Asa buys off Aram with temple silver instead of trusting God, and is rebuked: "the eyes of Yahweh run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong for those whose heart is right toward him."

stories.title: Elijah fed by ravens, and a widow's oil
stories.summary: Elijah announces a drought to king Ahab, then is fed by ravens at a brook until it dries up. Sent next to a foreign widow in Sidon who has almost nothing, he tells her to feed him first — and her jar of flour and oil never runs empty through the whole famine. When her son later dies, Elijah prays and the boy revives.

stories.title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
stories.summary: Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal to a contest: whichever god sends fire to consume the sacrifice is the true God. Baal answers with silence all day; Elijah's water-soaked altar is consumed instantly when he prays, and the watching crowd falls on their faces crying, "Yahweh, he is God."

stories.title: The battle is not yours but God's
stories.summary: A vast coalition marches on Judah. King Jehoshaphat gathers the nation to fast and pray — "we don't know what to do, but our eyes are on you" — and a Levite answers with God's word: the battle is not theirs but God's; they need only stand and watch. Jehoshaphat sends singers ahead of the army praising God's steadfast love, and the enemy destroys itself.

stories.title: Elijah at Horeb
stories.summary: Fleeing Jezebel's death threat after his victory on Carmel, an exhausted Elijah asks God to let him die. God instead feeds him, lets him walk forty days to Horeb, and reveals himself not in wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice — reminding Elijah that seven thousand in Israel have never bowed to Baal.

stories.title: Naboth's vineyard
stories.summary: Ahab sulks when Naboth refuses to sell his family's vineyard, so Jezebel arranges false charges that get Naboth stoned to death, letting Ahab simply take the land. Elijah meets Ahab at the vineyard with God's sentence on his house — and Ahab, humbled, has the judgment delayed rather than canceled.

stories.title: Elijah taken up to heaven
stories.summary: Knowing his time is near, Elijah asks Elisha what he can do for him before he goes; Elisha asks for a double portion of his spirit. A chariot of fire separates them and Elijah is carried up in a whirlwind. Elisha picks up the fallen mantle, strikes the Jordan with it, and the waters part for him too.

stories.title: The widow's oil
stories.summary: A prophet's widow, about to lose her sons to her creditors, has nothing left but a small jar of oil. Elisha tells her to borrow every empty container she can and start pouring; the oil keeps flowing until the last jar is full, enough to pay the debt and live on.

stories.title: The Shunammite woman's son
stories.summary: A well-off woman in Shunem builds Elisha a room on her roof. In return he promises her the son she never thought she'd have. Years later the boy dies suddenly; she rides straight to Elisha, who comes and stretches himself over the child until he sneezes and opens his eyes.

stories.title: Naaman healed
stories.summary: Naaman, an Aramean army commander with leprosy, hears of a prophet in Israel from a captured servant girl. He arrives expecting a grand ceremony and is told instead to wash seven times in the Jordan. Insulted, he almost leaves — until his servants talk him into it, and he comes up clean, declaring there is no God but the God of Israel. Elisha's servant Gehazi then chases Naaman down for a gift, and takes the leprosy with it.

stories.title: The chariots of fire
stories.summary: Aram sends an army by night to capture Elisha, and his servant panics at the sight of it. Elisha prays, and the servant's eyes are opened to see the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. Elisha then asks God to strike the enemy army with blindness, leads them into Samaria, and sends them home fed rather than killed.

stories.title: The siege of Samaria lifted
stories.summary: Aram's siege has driven Samaria to starvation and cannibalism. Elisha announces that by the next day food will be cheap again, and an officer scoffs. That night God makes the Aramean army hear the sound of a great host and flee, leaving everything behind; four lepers find the empty camp and bring the news, and the officer is trampled in the rush to the gate, exactly as Elisha said.

stories.title: Jehu and the death of Jezebel
stories.summary: A young prophet anoints the army commander Jehu king, charging him to wipe out Ahab's house and avenge the prophets Jezebel killed. Jehu drives to Jezreel, kills Ahab's son Joram, and orders Jezebel thrown from her window. By the time anyone goes to bury her, the dogs have left only her skull, feet, and hands — as Elijah had said.

stories.title: Joash and Zechariah
stories.summary: Hidden as an infant and crowned at seven by the priest Jehoiada, Joash does right as long as Jehoiada lives and restores the temple. But after the old priest dies, Joash listens to other officials and turns to idols. When Jehoiada's own son Zechariah rebukes him, Joash has him stoned in the temple court. Zechariah's dying words: "May Yahweh see, and avenge."

stories.title: The death of Elisha
stories.summary: Elisha, dying, has king Jehoash shoot an arrow out the window as a sign of victory over Aram, then rebukes him for striking the ground only three times instead of pressing on. After Elisha is buried, a body hurriedly thrown into his tomb touches his bones and the man comes back to life.

stories.title: Jonah flees, and the fish
stories.summary: Told to preach against Nineveh, Jonah instead books passage in the opposite direction. Yahweh sends a storm so violent the sailors throw cargo overboard and finally, at Jonah's own suggestion, throw him into the sea -- and the storm instantly stops. Yahweh sends a great fish to swallow him, and from its belly Jonah prays, remembering Yahweh even from what feels like the edge of death. After three days the fish vomits him onto dry land.

stories.title: Jonah and Nineveh
stories.summary: Given a second chance, Jonah goes to Nineveh and preaches one line: forty days until the city is overthrown. Remarkably, the whole city -- king included -- repents in sackcloth and ashes, and Yahweh relents. Jonah is furious rather than glad, admitting this mercy is exactly why he fled in the first place. Sulking outside the city, he's given shade by a plant, then angry all over again when it withers -- and Yahweh uses his misplaced grief over a plant to ask why he can't grieve for a hundred and twenty thousand people instead.

stories.title: Uzziah's pride
stories.summary: As long as Uzziah sought God he prospered, and his fame spread far. But once he was strong, his heart was lifted up: he walked into the temple to burn incense, a thing reserved for priests. Confronted by eighty priests, he raged at them with the censer still in his hand — and leprosy broke out on his forehead. He lived in isolation, cut off from the house of Yahweh, the rest of his life.

stories.title: Hosea's marriage
stories.summary: Yahweh tells Hosea to marry Gomer, a woman who will be unfaithful to him, as a living picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to God. Their children are given names that are themselves prophecies of judgment -- Jezreel, Lo-Ruhamah ("not pitied"), Lo-Ammi ("not my people"). When Gomer eventually leaves him for other lovers, Yahweh tells Hosea to buy her back and love her again -- exactly as Yahweh continues loving an unfaithful Israel.

stories.title: Amos confronts Amaziah
stories.summary: When Amos prophesies Israel's coming exile at the royal sanctuary in Bethel, the priest Amaziah reports him to the king and tells him to go back to Judah and prophesy there instead. Amos answers that he was never trained to be a prophet -- he was a shepherd and fig farmer until Yahweh took him from the flock and sent him -- and refuses to stop.

stories.title: Isaiah's call
stories.summary: In the year King Uzziah dies, Isaiah sees Yahweh high and lifted up in the temple, with seraphim calling "Holy, holy, holy" to one another until the door frames shake. Overwhelmed by his own uncleanness before God's holiness, he is purified by a coal from the altar — then volunteers the instant Yahweh asks who will go: "Here I am. Send me!"

stories.title: The fall of Israel
stories.summary: After two centuries of kings who led the northern kingdom into idolatry, Assyria captures Samaria and carries Israel away. The account stops the narrative to explain why: they had worshiped other gods, ignored every prophet God sent, and finally were removed from the land — leaving only Judah in the south.

stories.title: Hezekiah's Passover
stories.summary: In his first month as king, Hezekiah reopens and cleanses the temple his father had shut, then invites all Israel — north and south — to Jerusalem for a Passover the nation hasn't kept properly in generations. Many come unprepared and eat it anyway; Hezekiah prays that the good Yahweh will pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God, and God heals the people.

stories.title: Hezekiah and Sennacherib
stories.summary: Sennacherib of Assyria takes Judah's fortified cities and sends messengers to mock Hezekiah's trust in God. Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter out before Yahweh and prays that the nations may know he alone is God. That night God's angel strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib withdraws.

stories.title: Hezekiah's illness
stories.summary: Told by Isaiah to set his house in order because he will die, Hezekiah turns to the wall and weeps and prays. Before Isaiah has even left the palace, God sends him back: fifteen years added, and as a sign, the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz moves ten steps backward.

stories.title: Manasseh's repentance
stories.summary: Manasseh leads Judah into worse idolatry than the nations Israel had driven out — altars to other gods inside the temple itself. Assyria takes him to Babylon with a hook in his nose and in chains. There, in distress, he humbles himself and prays; God brings him back to Jerusalem, and Manasseh spends his last years tearing out the idols he had built.

stories.title: Jeremiah's call
stories.summary: In the thirteenth year of King Josiah, Yahweh tells Jeremiah he was appointed a prophet to the nations before he was even born. Jeremiah protests that he's too young and doesn't know how to speak; Yahweh touches his mouth, puts words in it, and tells him not to be afraid -- he is being sent to uproot and tear down, but also to build and to plant.

stories.title: Josiah and the Book of the Law
stories.summary: During temple repairs the high priest finds the lost Book of the Law. When it is read to king Josiah, he tears his clothes, realizing how far Judah has drifted. The prophetess Huldah confirms the coming judgment but says it will not fall in Josiah's lifetime because his heart was tender. Josiah gathers the nation, renews the covenant, and tears down every idol and high place in the land.

stories.title: The potter's house and the price of the message
stories.summary: Yahweh sends Jeremiah to watch a potter reshape a marred vessel into a new one -- a picture of his power over the nation. Jeremiah's actual preaching costs him: after a temple sermon warning Jerusalem it could be destroyed like Shiloh, the priests and prophets seize him and demand his death. He tells them plainly that killing him will bring innocent blood on the city, and is spared, though the message that burns in his bones like fire never stops costing him.

stories.title: Baruch's scroll
stories.summary: Jeremiah dictates all his prophecies to his scribe Baruch, who writes them on a scroll. When King Jehoiakim hears it read, he cuts off each section with a penknife and burns it in a brazier, unmoved. Yahweh has Jeremiah dictate it again to Baruch, with more added -- the burned scroll didn't burn the message. Around this same time, Jeremiah tells Baruch not to seek great things for himself in the coming catastrophe, only to be grateful his life will be spared.

stories.title: Daniel and the king's food
stories.summary: Carried to Babylon as young nobles of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah are renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and enrolled to be trained for the king's service. Daniel refuses to defile himself with the king's rich food and wine, and asks to be tested on vegetables and water instead. After ten days the four look healthier than everyone else, and God gives all four wisdom beyond every magician and enchanter in the kingdom.

stories.title: Nebuchadnezzar's dream
stories.summary: Troubled by a dream he refuses to describe, Nebuchadnezzar orders all his wise men executed when none can both tell him the dream and interpret it. Daniel asks for time, then prays with his three friends, and the secret is revealed to him in a night vision. He tells the king of a towering statue of decreasing precious metals, struck down by a stone that becomes a mountain filling the whole earth -- a picture of earthly kingdoms giving way to one that will never be destroyed. The king falls before Daniel and promotes him to rule over the whole province of Babylon.

stories.title: Ezekiel's call
stories.summary: Among the exiles by the river Chebar, Ezekiel sees a vision of Yahweh's glory -- a storm of fire, wheels within wheels, living creatures, and above it all a throne like sapphire. He falls on his face; a voice tells him to stand, calls him "son of man," and sends him to a rebellious people. He's told to eat a scroll of lament before he can speak it, then made a watchman: responsible to warn Israel of coming judgment, though the outcome is on their own heads if they refuse to listen.

stories.title: Ezekiel's symbolic acts
stories.summary: Ezekiel acts out Jerusalem's coming siege with his own body -- laying siege to a clay tile of the city, lying bound on his side for the number of years of Israel's and Judah's sin, eating rationed food. Later, told his wife will die suddenly and he is forbidden to mourn her publicly, he obeys -- and when the exiles ask why, he tells them Jerusalem's fall will be a grief too great for even that kind of mourning.

stories.title: The fiery furnace
stories.summary: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image and commands everyone to bow to it. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse, telling the king their God is able to deliver them -- but even if he doesn't, they still won't bow. Furious, Nebuchadnezzar has the furnace heated seven times hotter and has them thrown in bound. He looks in and sees four men walking unharmed in the flames, the fourth like a son of the gods. The three come out without so much as the smell of smoke on them, and Nebuchadnezzar blesses their God publicly.

stories.title: Jeremiah in the cistern
stories.summary: With Jerusalem under siege, Jeremiah's warnings that resistance is futile are called treason. The city's officials get King Zedekiah's permission and lower Jeremiah into a muddy cistern to die. Ebed-Melech, an Ethiopian official in the king's house, is the only one who speaks up for him -- he gets permission to pull Jeremiah out before he starves, using old rags to pad the ropes under his arms.

stories.title: Nebuchadnezzar's madness
stories.summary: Boasting over the great Babylon he has built by his own power, Nebuchadnezzar is struck by the very judgment a dream had already warned him about: his mind is taken from him and he lives like an animal in the fields for seven years. At the end of that time his understanding returns as he lifts his eyes to heaven and praises the Most High -- "those who walk in pride he is able to abase." His kingdom is restored to him.

stories.title: The fall of Jerusalem
stories.summary: Zedekiah rebels against Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar's army besieges Jerusalem for two years until the food runs out. The city is broken into, the temple and palace are burned, the walls are pulled down, and the people are carried off to Babylon. Zedekiah watches his sons killed, then is blinded and led away in chains.

stories.title: Gedaliah assassinated
stories.summary: After Jerusalem falls, the Babylonians appoint Gedaliah governor over the ruins of Judah, and Jeremiah goes to live under his protection along with the remnant left in the land. Within months, Ishmael son of Nethaniah -- of the royal line, and apparently resentful of a governor not descended from David -- assassinates Gedaliah and the men with him, throwing the fragile remaining community into panic.

stories.title: Flight to Egypt
stories.summary: Fearing Babylonian reprisal for Gedaliah's murder, the remaining leaders ask Jeremiah to seek Yahweh's word on whether to flee to Egypt. He tells them plainly to stay in the land. They refuse, accuse him of being manipulated by Baruch, and force both of them to Egypt anyway -- disobeying the very voice they claimed to be seeking.

stories.title: The writing on the wall
stories.summary: Belshazzar throws a great feast using the sacred vessels taken from Jerusalem's temple, and a disembodied hand appears and writes on the palace wall. None of his wise men can read it; Daniel is called in and interprets it without hesitation: God has numbered Belshazzar's kingdom and brought it to an end, weighed him and found him wanting, and is dividing his kingdom to the Medes and Persians. That same night, Belshazzar is killed.

stories.title: The valley of dry bones
stories.summary: Yahweh sets Ezekiel down in a valley full of dry bones and asks, "can these bones live?" Ezekiel prophesies as commanded, and the bones come together, grow flesh, and breathe -- an exceedingly great army rising from what had been total despair. Yahweh explains: the bones are all Israel, who have said "our hope is lost." He will open their graves, bring them back to their own land, and put his own Spirit in them.

stories.title: Daniel in the lions' den
stories.summary: Under Darius the Mede, Daniel's integrity draws envy from the other officials, who trick the king into signing a decree forbidding prayer to anyone but himself for thirty days -- knowing Daniel prays toward Jerusalem three times daily regardless. Daniel keeps praying exactly as before. Darius, forced by his own unchangeable law, has Daniel thrown to the lions, and spends a sleepless night hoping he survives. At dawn Daniel is found unharmed -- "my God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths" -- and Darius decrees that all his kingdom tremble before the God of Daniel.

stories.title: The decree of Cyrus
stories.summary: Chronicles ends where the exile began to lift. After seventy years, exactly as Jeremiah had said, Cyrus king of Persia issues a proclamation: Yahweh has charged him to build a house in Jerusalem, and any of God's people who wishes may go up. The last words of the Hebrew Bible's history are an open road home.

stories.title: The first return and the temple's foundation
stories.summary: Zerubbabel and the priest Jeshua lead the first wave of exiles home and rebuild the altar despite their fear of the surrounding peoples, restoring daily sacrifice before the temple itself is even begun. A year later the foundation is laid with trumpets, cymbals, and singing—old men who remembered the first temple weep aloud while everyone else shouts for joy, until the two sounds can no longer be told apart.

stories.title: Opposition halts the work
stories.summary: Local adversaries offer to help build the temple, are refused, and turn to discouragement, hired counselors, and finally a letter to the Persian king accusing Jerusalem of rebellion. The king orders the work stopped by force, and it sits idle for years, until Darius comes to the throne.

stories.title: The temple finished and dedicated
stories.summary: Encouraged by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, Zerubbabel and Jeshua resume building. The governor Tattenai questions their authority and writes to Darius, who searches the royal archives, confirms Cyrus's original decree, and orders the Persian treasury to fund the work instead of hindering it. The temple is finished and dedicated with sacrifices, and the returned exiles keep the Passover together for the first time since coming home.

stories.title: Ezra returns to teach the law
stories.summary: Decades later, Ezra—a priest and scribe who has set his heart to study, live, and teach Yahweh's law—leads a second return from Babylon under a sweeping grant of authority from king Artaxerxes. He gathers priests and Levites for the journey, refuses a royal military escort because he has already told the king that God's hand protects those who seek him, and arrives safely in Jerusalem with the temple treasures intact.

stories.title: Ezra's grief over intermarriage
stories.summary: Ezra learns that the returned exiles, priests and leaders included, have intermarried with the surrounding nations in violation of the law. He tears his robe, pulls out his own hair, and falls on his knees in a public prayer of confession before a crowd that gathers to weep with him. The people covenant to put away the foreign entanglements, and over several months the matter is investigated family by family.

stories.title: Nehemiah's burden for Jerusalem
stories.summary: Nehemiah, cupbearer to king Artaxerxes in the Persian capital of Susa, asks his brother for news of Jerusalem and learns the wall lies broken and the gates burned, more than a century after the first return. He sits down and weeps, then fasts and prays for days, confessing his people's sin and asking God to grant him favor with the king.

stories.title: Nehemiah is sent to rebuild
stories.summary: The king notices Nehemiah's sad face and asks what troubles him. Nehemiah, silently praying even as he answers, asks leave to go and rebuild the city of his fathers' tombs—and the king grants it, with letters of safe passage and timber for the gates. Three days after arriving in Jerusalem, Nehemiah rides out by night to inspect the ruined walls himself before telling anyone his plan.

stories.title: Building with a sword in hand
stories.summary: Sanballat mocks the rebuilding as the work of feeble Jews, and he and his allies conspire to attack Jerusalem and stop the work by force. Nehemiah sets a guard, arms the people by family, and keeps half of them working while the other half stands ready with spears and shields—trusting that God will fight for them if the trumpet sounds.

stories.title: Nehemiah cancels the people's debts
stories.summary: While the wall goes up, the poor cry out—mortgaging fields and selling their own children into debt slavery to their wealthier countrymen just to eat. Nehemiah is angry, confronts the nobles publicly, and demands they return what they've taken and stop charging interest. They agree on the spot, and Nehemiah adds that he himself, unlike governors before him, has never taken the governor's allowance from the people.

stories.title: The wall finished in fifty-two days
stories.summary: With the wall nearly done, Sanballat tries four times to lure Nehemiah away to a meeting meant to harm him, then sends an open letter threatening to report him to the king for rebellion. Nehemiah refuses each time and sees through a hired false prophet sent to frighten him into hiding. The wall is finished in just fifty-two days, and even Jerusalem's enemies recognize that the work was done by God.

stories.title: Ezra reads the law to the people
stories.summary: With the wall finished, the whole assembly gathers as one and asks Ezra to bring out the Book of the Law. He reads it aloud from early morning until midday while the people listen standing, and when they hear it they weep—until Nehemiah and Ezra tell them the day is holy, not for grief, and that the joy of Yahweh is their strength. They keep the Feast of Booths with a gladness Israel hadn't known since the days of Joshua, then gather again in sackcloth to confess their sins and recount everything God has done for them since Abraham, sealing a fresh written covenant.

stories.title: Nehemiah's final reforms
stories.summary: After time away in Persia, Nehemiah returns to Jerusalem to find how quickly things slipped: the priest Eliashib has given his ally Tobiah a room inside the temple itself, the Levites have gone unpaid and scattered back to their fields, merchants trade openly on the Sabbath, and the people are again intermarrying with surrounding nations. Nehemiah throws Tobiah's belongings out of the temple, restores the Levites' portions, shuts the city gates for the Sabbath, and confronts the offenders directly—closing the book with a final prayer: "Remember me, my God, for good."

stories.title: Vashti deposed
stories.summary: At a lavish feast in Susa, King Ahasuerus commands Queen Vashti to display her beauty before his guests. She refuses, and the king's advisors — fearing every wife in the empire will follow her example — persuade him to depose her by irrevocable decree, opening the search for a new queen.

stories.title: Esther becomes queen
stories.summary: Mordecai's orphaned cousin Esther is taken into the king's harem and, on his instruction, tells no one she is a Jew. She wins favor with everyone who sees her and is crowned queen in Vashti's place. Soon after, Mordecai overhears two eunuchs plotting to kill the king, reports it through Esther, and the plot is foiled and recorded — though Mordecai goes unrewarded for it.

stories.title: Haman's plot
stories.summary: The king promotes Haman above all his other officials, and everyone bows to him — except Mordecai, who won't. Haman's fury curdles into a plan to destroy not just Mordecai but every Jew in the empire; he casts lots for the date, pays for the king's permission, and sends out a sealed decree ordering their annihilation in a single day.

stories.title: "For such a time as this"
stories.summary: Mordecai tears his clothes and mourns publicly when the decree goes out. He sends word urging Esther to plead with the king for her people, but approaching the king uninvited is a capital offense even for the queen. Mordecai presses her: if she stays silent, deliverance will come from elsewhere and she will perish anyway — "who knows if you haven't come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" Esther asks all the Jews in Susa to fast with her for three days, then answers: "I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish."

stories.title: Esther's banquet and Haman's pride
stories.summary: Esther approaches the king unsummoned and he extends the golden scepter; instead of stating her request, she invites him and Haman to a private banquet, then a second one the next day. Haman leaves elated, until he passes Mordecai, who still won't bow — and at his wife's suggestion, has a gallows built to hang him on. That same sleepless night, the king has the royal chronicles read to him, discovers Mordecai was never rewarded for exposing the assassination plot, and — without realizing who he's describing — makes Haman personally lead Mordecai through the city in royal honor.

stories.title: Haman exposed and hanged
stories.summary: At her second banquet, Esther finally names her request: her life, and her people's — "we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed." When the king demands to know who dared, she names Haman to his face. Haman is hanged that same day on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

stories.title: The decree reversed
stories.summary: The king gives Esther Haman's estate and sets Mordecai over it. Esther pleads again, in tears, for her people, and the king lets Mordecai write a new decree in his name — one that cannot cancel Haman's, since Persian law forbids reversing a sealed decree, but that lets the Jews defend themselves and fight back when the day comes. Susa erupts in relief and celebration, and many among the surrounding peoples, afraid of the Jews, join them.

stories.title: Purim established
stories.summary: When the appointed day arrives, the Jews throughout the empire defend themselves and defeat those who rise against them, turning what was meant to be their destruction into deliverance. Mordecai and Esther write letters establishing the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar as Purim, an annual feast of remembrance, gladness, and gifts to the needy — and Mordecai, now second only to the king, spends his position seeking the good of his people.

stories.title: Job tested
stories.summary: Job, the greatest man of the east in wealth and family, is described to Satan by Yahweh as blameless and upright. Satan argues Job's faith is only rewarded loyalty, and is given permission to take everything: his oxen, sheep, camels, servants, and all ten of his children in a single day, then his own health, leaving him covered in sores and sitting in ashes. Job tears his robe and shaves his head, but refuses to curse God — "Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh's name." His wife urges him to curse God and die; he refuses. Three friends arrive and sit with him in silence for seven days, too stunned by his suffering to speak.

stories.title: Job's complaint and his friends' answers
stories.summary: Across many rounds of debate, Job's three friends insist his suffering must be punishment for some hidden sin — Eliphaz leads the argument. Job refuses to accept their explanation, protesting his innocence and demanding an answer from God directly, even while sinking into despair. In the middle of his darkest arguments he still declares, "I know that my Redeemer lives" — a flash of hope he can't yet explain or hold onto consistently.

stories.title: Yahweh answers out of the whirlwind
stories.summary: Yahweh finally answers Job — not with an explanation for his suffering, but with a sweeping tour of creation's wonders Job cannot explain or control: the foundations of the earth, the morning stars singing at creation, the wild animals no human can tame. Job doesn't get his questions answered. He repents anyway — not because he now understands, but because he has now seen God himself: "I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you."

stories.title: Job restored
stories.summary: Yahweh rebukes Eliphaz and his two companions for not speaking rightly about him, as Job had, and tells them to offer sacrifices while Job prays for them — which Yahweh accepts. Then Yahweh restores Job's fortunes, giving him double what he had before: more sheep, camels, oxen, and donkeys than at the start, seven more sons and three more daughters as beautiful as any in the land, and a long life to see four generations of his family.

stories.title: Gabriel's announcements
stories.summary: The angel Gabriel appears to the priest Zacharias in the temple, promising a son, John, to his barren, aging wife Elizabeth -- but Zacharias doubts and is struck mute until the birth. Six months later Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth pledged to Joseph, telling her she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear the Son of the Most High. Mary answers, "let it be done to me according to your word," then hurries to visit Elizabeth, whose unborn son leaps for joy at Mary's greeting. Mary responds with a song of praise -- the Magnificat -- celebrating God's reversal of the proud and the lowly.

stories.title: John the Baptist is born
stories.summary: Elizabeth gives birth, and when the neighbors assume the baby will be named after his father, she and the still-mute Zacharias both insist on the name John, exactly as the angel commanded. Zacharias's speech returns immediately, and he prophesies over his infant son -- that he will go before the Lord to prepare his way and give people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.

stories.title: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
stories.summary: A Roman census forces Joseph and the pregnant Mary to travel to Bethlehem, David's city, where Jesus is born and laid in a feeding trough for lack of room at the inn. That same night an angel announces the birth to shepherds in the fields nearby -- "good news of great joy" -- and a multitude of angels praises God. The shepherds hurry to see for themselves, then spread the word, while Mary quietly treasures everything that has happened.

stories.title: Jesus presented at the temple
stories.summary: Mary and Joseph bring the infant Jesus to Jerusalem to complete the rites required by the law. Simeon, promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Messiah, takes the child in his arms and blesses God -- "my eyes have seen your salvation" -- then warns Mary that her own soul will be pierced by what's coming. The prophetess Anna, who has spent decades in the temple in prayer and fasting, also recognizes the child and speaks of him to everyone looking for Jerusalem's redemption.

stories.title: The wise men and the flight to Egypt
stories.summary: Joseph, told in a dream that Mary's pregnancy is from the Holy Spirit, marries her and names the child Jesus as instructed. Wise men from the east, following a star, come to Jerusalem asking for the newborn King of the Jews; Herod, threatened, sends them to Bethlehem under the pretense of wanting to worship him too. The wise men find the child, worship him, and give gold, frankincense, and myrrh, then are warned in a dream not to return to Herod. Warned himself, Joseph flees with Mary and Jesus to Egypt, escaping just before Herod, enraged at being outwitted, kills every boy in Bethlehem two years old and under. After Herod's death the family returns, but settles in Nazareth rather than risk Judea under his son.

stories.title: The boy Jesus at the temple
stories.summary: At twelve, Jesus travels with his family to Jerusalem for Passover. When his parents head home, they don't realize he has stayed behind; after three days of searching, they find him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions that leave everyone amazed. To his mother's relief and confusion he answers simply: "didn't you know that I must be in my Father's house?" He returns with them to Nazareth and grows in wisdom and stature.

stories.title: John the Baptist's ministry
stories.summary: John preaches in the Judean wilderness, dressed in camel's hair and living on locusts and wild honey, calling people to repent because the kingdom of heaven is near. Crowds come from Jerusalem and beyond to be baptized in the Jordan, confessing their sins; he confronts the religious leaders who come only to be seen, and tells everyone that one far greater than him is coming, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.

stories.title: Jesus is baptized
stories.summary: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John, who objects that it should be the other way around. Jesus insists, "to fulfill all righteousness," and John agrees. As Jesus comes up out of the water, the heavens open, the Spirit descends on him like a dove, and a voice from heaven declares, "this is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."

stories.title: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
stories.summary: Led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Jesus fasts forty days and is tempted three times by the devil -- to turn stones to bread, to throw himself from the temple to force God's rescue, and to worship the devil in exchange for the world's kingdoms. Each time Jesus answers with Scripture rather than his own power, and the devil finally leaves him.

stories.title: The first disciples follow Jesus
stories.summary: John points two of his own disciples, including Andrew, to Jesus as "the Lamb of God." Andrew follows, then finds his brother Simon and brings him to Jesus, who renames him Peter. The next day Jesus calls Philip directly; Philip finds his skeptical friend Nathanael, whose doubt dissolves the moment Jesus reveals he already knew him, sitting under a fig tree before they'd even met.

stories.title: Water into wine at Cana
stories.summary: At a wedding in Cana, the wine runs out. Jesus's mother tells the servants to do whatever he says; he has them fill six stone jars with water, then has it drawn out and taken to the master of the feast, who is amazed to find the best wine has been saved for last. It's the first of Jesus's signs, and his disciples believe in him because of it.

stories.title: Jesus calls the fishermen
stories.summary: Teaching from Simon's boat on the lake of Gennesaret, Jesus tells him to put out into deep water and let down the nets, even though he's fished all night with nothing to show for it. The catch is so large the nets start breaking and both boats nearly sink. Overwhelmed, Peter falls at Jesus's knees, calling himself a sinful man -- but Jesus tells him not to be afraid: "from now on you will be catching people." Peter, Andrew, James, and John bring their boats to land and leave everything to follow him.

stories.title: The calling of Matthew
stories.summary: Passing a tax collection booth, Jesus tells the tax collector Matthew, "follow me" -- and he gets up immediately and follows. At a feast in Matthew's house full of tax collectors and other people the Pharisees considered sinners, the Pharisees ask why Jesus eats with such people. Jesus answers that it's the sick who need a doctor, not the healthy: "I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."

stories.title: The Sermon on the Mount
stories.summary: Seeing the crowds, Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches his disciples at length -- the Beatitudes ("blessed are the poor in spirit... the merciful... the peacemakers"), calling his followers salt and light, and insisting he came to fulfill the law, not abolish it, by pressing it deeper than outward behavior into the heart (anger as a seed of murder, lust as a seed of adultery, loving enemies instead of just neighbors). He teaches them to pray simply (the Lord's Prayer), to store up treasure in heaven rather than on earth, not to be anxious since God feeds the birds and clothes the flowers, not to judge others while ignoring their own faults, to ask/seek/knock in prayer, and to treat others as they want to be treated. He closes with the choice between a narrow gate and a wide one, and a wise builder whose house survives the storm because it's built on rock. The crowds are astonished -- he teaches with real authority, not like their scribes.

stories.title: The parable of the sower
stories.summary: Teaching a crowd from a boat, Jesus tells of a farmer scattering seed: some falls on the path and is eaten by birds, some on rocky soil and withers without root, some among thorns and is choked out, and some on good soil, yielding a huge harvest. Asked privately why he teaches in parables, he explains that the seed is the word of God and the soils are different ways people receive it -- distracted, shallow, choked by worry and riches, or genuinely fruitful.

stories.title: The good Samaritan
stories.summary: A legal expert, testing Jesus, asks what he must do to inherit eternal life; Jesus points him back to the law -- love God and love your neighbor -- and the man, looking to justify himself, asks "who is my neighbor?" Jesus answers with a story: a man is beaten and left half-dead on the Jericho road, and both a priest and a Levite -- men who should know the law best -- pass by on the other side. It's a Samaritan, someone from a people Jews despised, who stops, bandages his wounds, and pays for his care at an inn. Jesus asks which of the three was a neighbor, then tells the lawyer to go and do the same.

stories.title: The prodigal son
stories.summary: A younger son demands his inheritance early, leaves for a distant country, and squanders it all on reckless living until a famine leaves him feeding pigs and envying their food. Coming to his senses, he heads home to beg to be taken back as a hired servant -- but while he's still far off, his father sees him, runs to him, and embraces him before he can even finish his rehearsed apology, calling for a robe, a ring, and a celebration feast: "this son of mine was dead, and is alive again." The older son, who stayed and obeyed, refuses to join the celebration, resentful that his years of faithfulness were never celebrated like this. His father goes out to him too: "you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours" -- but this brother, once lost, had to be celebrated for coming home.

stories.title: Jesus calms the storm
stories.summary: Crossing the lake by boat, Jesus falls asleep in the stern while a violent storm fills the boat with water. His disciples wake him, panicked -- "don't you care that we are dying?" He rebukes the wind and says to the sea, "Peace! Be still!" and it goes suddenly, completely calm. More frightened by this than by the storm, the disciples ask each other what kind of man commands even the wind and the waves.

stories.title: Feeding the five thousand
stories.summary: A crowd of thousands follows Jesus to a remote place, and by evening the disciples want to send everyone off to buy food. Jesus tells them to feed the crowd themselves; all they have is five loaves and two fish. He blesses and breaks the food, the disciples distribute it, and everyone -- about five thousand men, plus women and children -- eats until full, with twelve baskets of leftovers. It's the one miracle told in all four Gospels.

stories.title: Jesus walks on water
stories.summary: After sending the crowds home, Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up a mountain alone to pray. Late that night, with the boat fighting a strong headwind, he comes to them walking on the sea; they scream, thinking he's a ghost, until he calls out, "Cheer up! It is I. Don't be afraid." Peter asks to come to him on the water and does, until he notices the wind and starts to sink -- "Lord, save me!" Jesus catches him immediately, asking why he doubted. Once they're both in the boat, the wind stops, and everyone worships him: "you are truly the Son of God."

stories.title: Peter's confession
stories.summary: At Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks who people say he is, then who the disciples themselves say he is. Peter answers, "you are the Christ, the Son of the living God" -- a revelation Jesus says could only have come from the Father. Jesus begins telling them plainly that he must suffer, be killed, and rise on the third day; Peter, appalled, tries to talk him out of it, and Jesus rebukes him sharply -- "get behind me, Satan" -- before telling all the disciples that following him means denying themselves and taking up a cross, because whoever tries to save their life will lose it.

stories.title: The Transfiguration
stories.summary: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a mountain, where he is transformed before them -- his face shining like the sun, his clothes dazzling white -- and Moses and Elijah appear, talking with him. Peter, overwhelmed, offers to build three shelters, but a bright cloud overshadows them and a voice says, "this is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased -- listen to him." The disciples fall down terrified; when they look up, only Jesus remains.

stories.title: Nicodemus and being born again
stories.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler of the Jews, comes to Jesus at night, acknowledging he must be a teacher sent from God. Jesus tells him no one can see God's kingdom without being "born again" -- born of water and the Spirit, not merely of flesh. Nicodemus can't understand how an old man could be born a second time; Jesus presses further, comparing the Spirit to wind that can't be seen but is unmistakably real, then explains why he came at all: "God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life."

stories.title: The woman at the well
stories.summary: Tired from traveling through Samaria, Jesus rests at Jacob's well and asks a Samaritan woman for a drink -- crossing two social lines at once, since Jews avoided Samaritans and men didn't speak alone with unfamiliar women. He offers her "living water" that permanently satisfies, then reveals he already knows she's had five husbands and isn't married to the man she's with now. Recognizing him as a prophet, she raises the old dispute over where God should be worshiped; Jesus tells her true worship is about spirit and truth, not location, and when she mentions the coming Messiah, he tells her plainly: "I am he." She leaves her water pot and runs to tell the whole town, and many Samaritans come to believe in him because of her testimony.

stories.title: Lazarus raised from the dead
