stories.summary: Jesus's friend Lazarus falls sick, and though he loves the family, Jesus deliberately delays two days before heading to Bethany -- by the time he arrives, Lazarus has been in the tomb four days. Martha meets him on the road, grieving but still confessing faith; Jesus tells her, "I am the resurrection and the life," and asks if she believes it. At the tomb, seeing Mary and the mourners weeping, Jesus himself weeps. He has the stone rolled away over Martha's protest about the smell, thanks the Father aloud for the crowd's sake, and calls out, "Lazarus, come out!" Lazarus walks out still wrapped in his graveclothes.

stories.title: Zacchaeus
stories.summary: Passing through Jericho, Jesus draws such a crowd that Zacchaeus, a short and wealthy chief tax collector, climbs a sycamore tree just to see him. Jesus stops, looks up, and invites himself to Zacchaeus's house -- to the crowd's disgust, since tax collectors were seen as collaborators and cheats. Zacchaeus responds on the spot: half his wealth to the poor, and fourfold repayment to anyone he's defrauded. Jesus declares that salvation has come to his house, "for the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost."

stories.title: The rich young ruler
stories.summary: A young man who has kept the commandments since his youth asks Jesus what he still lacks for eternal life. Jesus tells him to sell everything, give it to the poor, and follow him -- and the man leaves grieving, because he is very wealthy. Jesus tells his stunned disciples that it's easier for a camel to pass through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter God's kingdom, though what's impossible for people is possible for God.

stories.title: The triumphal entry
stories.summary: Approaching Jerusalem, Jesus sends two disciples ahead for a donkey and its colt, fulfilling Zechariah's prophecy of a king who comes humble, riding on a donkey. Crowds spread their cloaks and palm branches on the road and shout "Hosanna to the son of David!" as he enters the city, which is thrown into an uproar asking who he is. It's the beginning of his final week.

stories.title: The Last Supper
stories.summary: Jesus shares a final Passover meal with the twelve, telling them plainly that one of them will betray him -- each asks in turn, "it isn't me, is it, Lord?" He takes bread, gives thanks, breaks it, and says, "take, eat; this is my body," then the cup: "this is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the remission of sins." After singing a hymn, they leave for the Mount of Olives.

stories.title: Jesus washes his disciples' feet
stories.summary: During the same meal, Jesus gets up, wraps a towel around his waist, and washes his disciples' feet -- a servant's job. Peter objects, then overcorrects, wanting his hands and head washed too; Jesus tells him this act is an example to follow: "if I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet." He adds a new commandment -- to love one another as he has loved them, the mark by which everyone will know they are his disciples.

stories.title: Jesus comforts his disciples
stories.summary: Knowing what's coming, Jesus spends the rest of the meal comforting and preparing the disciples: "don't let your heart be troubled... I am the way, the truth, and the life," a promise of peace unlike anything the world gives, an image of himself as a vine and them as branches who can do nothing apart from him, and a warning that they'll have trouble in the world but can take heart, because he has overcome it.

stories.title: Gethsemane
stories.summary: In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John further with him, telling them his soul is sorrowful to the point of death. He prays three times, alone, that the coming suffering might pass -- "nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire" -- while the three keep falling asleep instead of keeping watch with him. He wakes them a final time: the hour has come, and his betrayer is near.

stories.title: Betrayal and arrest
stories.summary: Judas arrives with an armed crowd sent by the chief priests, identifying Jesus with a prearranged kiss. Jesus doesn't resist -- when one of his own strikes off the ear of the high priest's servant, Jesus tells him to put the sword away, pointing out he could call down legions of angels if he wanted rescue. He lets himself be taken, noting they came at him with weapons as if he were a criminal, though he'd taught openly in the temple every day. All the disciples run.

stories.title: Jesus before the council
stories.summary: Jesus is brought to Caiaphas the high priest, where the council searches for testimony to justify a death sentence, but the false witnesses can't even agree with each other. Jesus stays silent until Caiaphas demands, under oath, whether he is the Christ, the Son of God. Jesus answers plainly and adds that they will see him at God's right hand, coming on the clouds -- and Caiaphas tears his robes, calling it blasphemy. The council condemns him, and the guards spit on him, beat him, and mock him.

stories.title: Peter's denial
stories.summary: While Jesus is on trial inside, Peter waits in the courtyard outside. Three times he's recognized as one of Jesus's followers, and three times he denies it -- the last time with cursing and an oath. The moment he finishes, a rooster crows, and Peter remembers Jesus's own prediction that he would deny him three times before it did. He goes out and weeps bitterly.

stories.title: Judas's remorse
stories.summary: Seeing Jesus condemned, Judas is overcome with remorse and tries to return the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests, confessing he has betrayed innocent blood. They refuse to take responsibility -- "what is that to us? You see to it" -- so he throws the money into the temple and hangs himself. The priests, unwilling to put blood money into the treasury, use it to buy a field to bury foreigners in, later called the Field of Blood.

stories.title: Jesus before Pilate
stories.summary: Handed to the Roman governor Pilate, Jesus gives almost no answer to the accusations against him, leaving Pilate amazed. Trying to release him under a Passover custom of freeing one prisoner, Pilate offers the crowd a choice between Jesus and a notorious prisoner, Barabbas -- and, stirred up by the chief priests, they choose Barabbas and demand Jesus be crucified. Warned by his wife's troubling dream, Pilate senses Jesus's innocence but gives in to avoid a riot, washing his hands in a public disclaimer before having Jesus flogged and handed over to be crucified.

stories.title: The crucifixion
stories.summary: Soldiers mock Jesus with a crown of thorns and a scarlet robe before leading him to Golgotha, pressing Simon of Cyrene into carrying his cross. Crucified between two criminals, Jesus is mocked by passersby, priests, and one of the criminals -- but forgives his executioners ("Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing") and promises the other, repentant criminal paradise that same day. He entrusts his mother to John's care, and after three hours of darkness cries out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" before his final words -- "it is finished... Father, into your hands I commit my spirit" -- and dies. The temple curtain tears in two, the earth shakes, and a Roman centurion watching declares, "truly this was the Son of God."

stories.title: Jesus is buried
stories.summary: Joseph of Arimathea, a rich man and secret disciple, asks Pilate for Jesus's body, wraps it himself, and lays it in his own new tomb cut into the rock, rolling a great stone across the entrance. Mary Magdalene and another Mary sit watching, opposite the tomb. The next day, remembering Jesus's own prediction that he would rise on the third day, the chief priests get Pilate's permission to post a guard and seal the stone, determined to prevent any claim of resurrection.

stories.title: The empty tomb
stories.summary: At dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to the tomb and find it opened by an earthquake and an angel, whose appearance terrifies the guards into a dead faint. The angel tells the women Jesus has risen, just as he said, and sends them to tell the disciples. Running to spread the news, they meet Jesus himself, who greets them and repeats the instruction to go to Galilee. Meanwhile, the guards report everything to the chief priests, who bribe them to say the disciples stole the body while they slept.

stories.title: Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene
stories.summary: Weeping alone outside the empty tomb, Mary Magdalene sees a man she assumes is the gardener and asks where the body has been taken. He says just one word -- her name, "Mary" -- and she recognizes Jesus instantly, crying out "Rabboni!" He tells her not to cling to him, since he hasn't yet ascended, but to go tell the disciples. She becomes the first witness of the resurrection to carry the news.

stories.title: The road to Emmaus
stories.summary: Two disciples, including one named Cleopas, walk to the village of Emmaus discussing everything that has happened, joined by Jesus himself -- though they don't recognize him. He asks what they're discussing, then, hearing their grief and confusion, calls them slow to believe and walks them through the Scriptures, showing how the Christ had to suffer before entering his glory. Invited to stay for the evening, he takes bread, gives thanks, and breaks it -- and in that instant they recognize him, just before he vanishes. They rush back to Jerusalem the same hour to tell the others.

stories.title: Doubting Thomas
stories.summary: Thomas, absent when Jesus first appeared to the other disciples, refuses to believe without physical proof -- seeing and touching the wounds himself. A week later Jesus appears again, this time with Thomas present, and invites him to touch his hands and side directly. Thomas responds with the clearest confession in the Gospels: "my Lord and my God!" Jesus tells him that those who believe without seeing are the ones who will be blessed.

stories.title: The Great Commission
stories.summary: On a mountain in Galilee, the eleven remaining disciples meet the risen Jesus -- worshiping him, though some still doubt. He tells them all authority in heaven and earth has been given to him, and sends them out to make disciples of every nation, baptizing them and teaching them everything he commanded, with a final promise: "I am with you always, even to the end of the age."

stories.title: The ascension
stories.summary: Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany, lifts his hands, and blesses them -- and as he does, he is carried up into heaven. The disciples worship him and return to Jerusalem overflowing with joy, spending their time in the temple praising God, waiting for what he had promised would come next.

stories.title: Choosing Matthias
stories.summary: Back in Jerusalem after the ascension, the disciples devote themselves to prayer together with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers. Peter stands up before the group of about a hundred twenty believers and explains that Judas's betrayal and death leave his place among the twelve empty. Two candidates are put forward; after prayer, they cast lots, and it falls to Matthias, who is counted among the eleven apostles.

stories.title: Pentecost
stories.summary: On the day of Pentecost, a sound like a rushing wind fills the house where the disciples are gathered, and what looks like tongues of fire rests on each of them; they're filled with the Holy Spirit and begin speaking in other languages. Peter stands and preaches to the crowd that has gathered, explaining that this Jesus, whom they crucified, God has raised up and made both Lord and Christ. Cut to the heart, the crowd asks what they should do; Peter tells them to repent and be baptized for the forgiveness of sins. About three thousand are added that day, and the new believers devote themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread, and prayer -- sharing everything they have and growing daily.

stories.title: Peter heals a lame man
stories.summary: Going up to the temple to pray, Peter and John pass a man lame from birth, begging at the gate called Beautiful. Peter tells him, "I have no silver or gold, but what I have, I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk." He pulls the man up by the hand, and his feet and ankles are instantly strong -- he walks into the temple with them, leaping and praising God, to the astonishment of everyone who recognizes him as the beggar who used to sit there.

stories.title: Stephen's martyrdom
stories.summary: Stephen, one of seven men chosen to help the growing church, performs signs and argues with such wisdom that his opponents can't out-debate him -- so they get him falsely accused of blasphemy and dragged before the council. As he finishes a long defense retracing Israel's history, his accusers are enraged; Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looks up and sees Jesus standing at God's right hand. They drag him out of the city and stone him while a young man named Saul watches, holding the coats of the witnesses. Stephen dies praying, like Jesus before him, for his killers' forgiveness.

stories.title: Saul's conversion on the road to Damascus
stories.summary: Still breathing threats against the church, Saul is on his way to Damascus with authority to arrest believers when a blinding light stops him and a voice asks, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" It's Jesus himself. Blind for three days, Saul is found by a reluctant disciple named Ananias, who's told in a vision that this feared persecutor is God's chosen instrument to carry his name to the nations. Ananias lays hands on him; something like scales fall from Saul's eyes, and he's baptized, immediately beginning to preach the very faith he came to destroy.

stories.title: Peter and Cornelius
stories.summary: Cornelius, a devout Roman centurion, is told in a vision to send for Peter. The next day, Peter himself has a vision -- a sheet full of animals he's told to kill and eat, including foods forbidden under Jewish law. When he refuses, a voice tells him three times, "what God has cleansed, you must not call unclean." As he's puzzling over it, Cornelius's messengers arrive, and Peter goes with them, now understanding the vision was never about food: "God has shown me that I shouldn't call any man unholy or unclean." Preaching to Cornelius's household, Peter declares that God shows no favoritism between nations -- and while he's still speaking, the Holy Spirit falls on the Gentiles gathered there, exactly as it did on the disciples at Pentecost. Peter has them baptized on the spot, opening the church to the Gentile world.

stories.title: Paul's first missionary journey
stories.summary: At Antioch, the Holy Spirit tells the church leaders to set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work he has called them to; after fasting and prayer, they're sent off. Traveling through Cyprus and into Asia Minor, preaching in synagogues and facing both belief and violent opposition, Saul increasingly goes by his Roman name, Paul -- and increasingly leads. The journey establishes the pattern for everything that follows: preach first to the Jews, then to the Gentiles who respond, and press on despite real danger.

stories.title: The Jerusalem council
stories.summary: Some believers insist Gentile converts must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses to be saved. Paul and Barnabas dispute this sharply enough that the church sends them to Jerusalem to settle it with the apostles and elders. After much debate, Peter reminds everyone that God gave the Gentiles the Holy Spirit without distinction, "cleansing their hearts by faith" -- salvation is by grace, not a burden their own ancestors couldn't carry either. The council agrees, asking only that Gentile believers avoid a short list of specific practices, rather than the whole law -- a decision they describe as seeming good "to the Holy Spirit, and to us."

stories.title: The Philippian jailer
stories.summary: Arrested and beaten in Philippi, Paul and Silas spend midnight praying and singing hymns in prison instead of despairing -- until a sudden earthquake throws open every door and loosens every chain. The jailer wakes, assumes his prisoners have escaped, and draws his sword to kill himself rather than face the consequences, but Paul stops him: everyone is still there. Trembling, the jailer asks what he must do to be saved. Paul and Silas tell him to believe in the Lord Jesus -- and he and his entire household are baptized that same night.

stories.title: Paul at the Areopagus
stories.summary: Waiting in Athens and disturbed by the city's idols, Paul is invited to explain his teaching to the philosophers at the Areopagus. He starts from common ground -- an altar he'd noticed inscribed "TO AN UNKNOWN GOD" -- and announces that this unknown God is the one who made the world, doesn't live in temples, and isn't far from anyone: "in him we live, move, and have our being." He calls his listeners to repent, since God has fixed a day of judgment and given proof of it by raising Jesus from the dead. Some mock the idea of resurrection; a few believe.

stories.title: Paul's arrest in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Back in Jerusalem, Paul is seized in the temple by a mob who wrongly believe he's brought a Gentile past the temple's sacred boundary, and is beaten nearly to death before Roman soldiers pull him out and arrest him. The following night, Jesus himself stands by Paul and tells him to take courage: just as he has testified about him in Jerusalem, he must testify in Rome too -- a promise that sets up everything left in Acts. Years of trials before the governors Felix and Festus and King Agrippa follow, none of them finding real grounds for a charge; when Agrippa half-jokes that Paul is nearly persuading him to become a Christian, Paul answers that he wishes everyone listening could become as he is, chains excepted.

stories.title: Shipwrecked on the way to Rome
stories.summary: Having appealed to Caesar, Paul is sent toward Rome by ship and sails into a storm so violent that all hope of survival is lost -- until an angel tells him no lives will be lost, only the ship. Fourteen days adrift, the ship finally runs aground and breaks apart in the surf, but everyone reaches the island of Malta safely, exactly as Paul had said. There, gathering firewood, a viper bites his hand; when he simply shakes it off unharmed, the islanders decide he must be a god.

stories.title: Paul in Rome
stories.summary: After finally reaching Rome, Paul spends two full years under house arrest at his own expense, welcoming everyone who comes to him and preaching the kingdom of God and the Lord Jesus Christ with total boldness, completely unhindered -- the note Acts ends on, the gospel having traveled from a locked upper room in Jerusalem to the capital of the empire.

stories.title: John's vision on Patmos
stories.summary: Exiled on the island of Patmos "for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ," John is caught up in the Spirit on the Lord's day and hears a voice like a trumpet behind him. Turning, he sees seven golden lampstands and, among them, one like a son of man -- robed, hair white as snow, eyes like fire, feet like burnished brass, a sword from his mouth, his face shining like the sun. John falls at his feet like a dead man. The risen Christ lays his hand on him: "Don't be afraid... I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever... I have the keys of Death and of Hades." He is commissioned to write what he has seen, what is, and what will be, and sent with letters to seven churches in Asia -- the vision that becomes the whole book of Revelation.

lifeEvents.title: Sent by God to meet Moses
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh tells Aaron to go into the wilderness to meet his brother.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes Moses' spokesman
lifeEvents.description: God tells Moses that Aaron, who can speak well, will be his mouth.

lifeEvents.title: Speaks for Moses before Pharaoh
lifeEvents.description: He repeats Yahweh's demand to Pharaoh through the escalating plagues.

lifeEvents.title: Keeps the first Passover
lifeEvents.description: He and Moses lead Israel through the night of the tenth plague.

lifeEvents.title: Holds up Moses' hands
lifeEvents.description: When Moses' arms grow heavy on the hilltop, Aaron holds one side up until Joshua wins the battle.

lifeEvents.title: Makes the golden calf
lifeEvents.description: Pressured by the people, he collects their gold and fashions it into an idol.

lifeEvents.title: Ordained as priest
lifeEvents.description: He and his sons offer the first sacrifices; fire from Yahweh consumes the offering and the camp shouts.

lifeEvents.title: Loses Nadab and Abihu
lifeEvents.description: Fire from Yahweh kills both sons in front of him for an offering he never commanded. Aaron says nothing.

lifeEvents.title: Sees Miriam struck with leprosy
lifeEvents.description: He and Moses watch it happen the moment the cloud lifts from the Tent.

lifeEvents.title: Stands with Moses against Korah
lifeEvents.description: Korah accuses them both of taking too much power.

lifeEvents.title: Barred from the promised land
lifeEvents.description: He shares in the consequence of Moses striking the rock instead of speaking to it.

lifeEvents.title: Dies on Mount Hor
lifeEvents.description: His garments pass to Eleazar; all Israel mourns him thirty days.

lifeEvents.title: Joins Daniel's food test
lifeEvents.description: Is renamed and trained for the king's service alongside Daniel.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses to bow and walks out of the furnace unharmed
lifeEvents.description: Refuses to worship Nebuchadnezzar's image and survives the furnace.

lifeEvents.title: Brings the firstborn of his flock
lifeEvents.description: A keeper of sheep, he brings the fat portions of the firstborn, and God accepts it.

lifeEvents.title: Killed in the field
lifeEvents.description: His brother kills him, and his blood cries out from the ground.

lifeEvents.title: Ordained a priest
lifeEvents.description: He is set apart alongside his father and brothers.

lifeEvents.title: Dies offering unauthorized fire
lifeEvents.description: He and his brother Nadab offer incense God never commanded, and are killed instantly.

lifeEvents.title: Wins by relying on Yahweh
lifeEvents.description: Outnumbered and outflanked by Jeroboam, warns Israel not to fight against God, and Judah prevails.

lifeEvents.title: Called out of Haran
lifeEvents.description: Told to leave his country, his relatives and his father's house for a land he will be shown.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Lot first choice of the land
lifeEvents.description: The elder yields to the younger to keep peace between their herdsmen.

lifeEvents.title: Counts the stars, and believes
lifeEvents.description: Promised offspring beyond counting, he believes God, and it is credited to him as righteousness.

lifeEvents.title: Takes Hagar, and Ishmael is born
lifeEvents.description: Ten years into waiting, Sarai's plan produces a son who is not the promised one.

lifeEvents.title: Renamed Abraham
lifeEvents.description: God renames him father of many nations and gives circumcision as the covenant sign.

lifeEvents.title: Bargains with God for Sodom
lifeEvents.description: Dust and ashes, he presses God down from fifty righteous to ten.

lifeEvents.title: Isaac is born
lifeEvents.description: The promise arrives twenty-five years after it was made.

lifeEvents.title: Sends Hagar and Ishmael away
lifeEvents.description: Distressed, he does it at Sarah's insistence and God's word — and God provides for them.

lifeEvents.title: Offers Isaac on Moriah
lifeEvents.description: He raises the knife over the son he waited a lifetime for, and God provides the ram.

lifeEvents.title: Buries Sarah at Machpelah
lifeEvents.description: He mourns her, then buys the cave — the first ground in the promised land he owns.

lifeEvents.title: Sends for a wife for Isaac
lifeEvents.description: He sends his servant back to his own people, and the servant is led to Rebekah.

lifeEvents.title: Dies at a hundred and seventy-five
lifeEvents.description: Isaac and Ishmael bury him beside Sarah.

lifeEvents.title: Avenges Tamar
lifeEvents.description: Waits two years, then has his servants kill Amnon at a feast.

lifeEvents.title: Reconciled with David
lifeEvents.description: Returns from exile and is received back by his father.

lifeEvents.title: Steals the hearts of Israel
lifeEvents.description: Stations himself at the city gate, telling every petitioner he would judge their case better than the king.

lifeEvents.title: Dies caught in an oak tree
lifeEvents.description: His head catches in the branches while fleeing; Joab kills him against David's express order.

lifeEvents.title: Takes forbidden plunder
lifeEvents.description: He secretly keeps silver, gold, and a robe from Jericho that had been devoted to destruction, and buries it under his tent.

lifeEvents.title: Found out and stoned
lifeEvents.description: His sin is why Israel was defeated at Ai; once found, he confesses and is stoned.

lifeEvents.title: Formed from the dust
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh God shapes the man from the ground and breathes life into him.

lifeEvents.title: Names the animals, and is given Eve
lifeEvents.description: No suitable helper is found among the creatures, so God makes the woman.

lifeEvents.title: Eats the fruit
lifeEvents.description: Eve gives him some of the fruit and he eats it too.

lifeEvents.title: Put out of the garden
lifeEvents.description: Sent out to work ground that now resists him, with cherubim barring the way back.

lifeEvents.title: Declares himself king
lifeEvents.description: Exalts himself and prepares chariots and runners before David has named a successor.

lifeEvents.title: Watches Elijah's contest with Baal's prophets
lifeEvents.description: Present when fire falls and the people declare Yahweh is God.

lifeEvents.title: Takes Naboth's vineyard
lifeEvents.description: Sulks until Jezebel has Naboth killed, then takes the land for himself.

lifeEvents.title: Deposes Vashti for refusing his summons
lifeEvents.description: Deposes Queen Vashti by irrevocable decree after she refuses to appear before his feast.

lifeEvents.title: Chooses Esther as queen without learning she is a Jew
lifeEvents.description: Loves Esther more than all the other women and crowns her queen.

lifeEvents.title: Grants Haman authority to destroy the Jews
lifeEvents.description: Gives Haman his signet ring and authority to do as he sees fit with "a certain people."

lifeEvents.title: Has Haman hanged after Esther exposes his plot
lifeEvents.description: Orders Haman hanged on the gallows built for Mordecai once Esther names him as the enemy.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Esther Haman's estate and lets a new decree be written
lifeEvents.description: Gives Esther Haman's house and lets Mordecai write a decree letting the Jews defend themselves.

lifeEvents.title: Forces his sister Tamar
lifeEvents.description: Obsessed with her, tricks her into his room and rapes her.

lifeEvents.title: Killed by Absalom's servants
lifeEvents.description: Struck down at a feast two years after raping Tamar.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses to stop prophesying when ordered to leave
lifeEvents.description: Answers Amaziah's demand to leave Bethel by explaining Yahweh took him from shepherding to prophesy.

lifeEvents.title: Follows Jesus and brings his brother Peter
lifeEvents.description: Is the first to follow Jesus after hearing John call him the Lamb of God.

lifeEvents.title: Leaves his nets to follow Jesus full-time
lifeEvents.description: Leaves everything after the miraculous catch of fish.

lifeEvents.title: Cries to Yahweh against a vast army
lifeEvents.description: "There is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength."

lifeEvents.title: Trusts Aram instead of God, and is rebuked
lifeEvents.description: Buys off Syria with temple silver; a seer tells him he has done foolishly.

lifeEvents.title: Hired to curse Israel
lifeEvents.description: A Moabite king pays him to curse the people camped at his border.

lifeEvents.title: His donkey speaks
lifeEvents.description: She sees the angel of Yahweh blocking the road before he does, and asks him what she's done to deserve being struck.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses Israel instead of cursing them
lifeEvents.description: Every time he opens his mouth to curse, blessing comes out — including a glimpse of a king far in Israel's future.

lifeEvents.title: Is released in Jesus's place
lifeEvents.description: Is freed by the crowd's demand while Jesus is condemned instead.

lifeEvents.title: Summoned by Deborah
lifeEvents.description: He agrees to fight only if she comes with him.

lifeEvents.title: Routs Sisera's army
lifeEvents.description: Sisera flees on foot; the honor of finishing him goes to a woman instead.

lifeEvents.title: Partners with Paul on the first missionary journey
lifeEvents.description: Is set apart alongside Paul by the Holy Spirit for missionary work.

lifeEvents.title: Supports Paul at the Jerusalem council
lifeEvents.description: Joins Paul in disputing the circumcision requirement for Gentiles.

lifeEvents.title: Writes Jeremiah's prophecies onto a scroll, twice
lifeEvents.description: Serves as Jeremiah's scribe and is told not to seek great things for himself.

lifeEvents.title: Is carried to Egypt with Jeremiah
lifeEvents.description: Is blamed for influencing Jeremiah and forced to Egypt along with him.

lifeEvents.title: Taken by David
lifeEvents.description: Sent for while her husband Uriah is away at war; becomes pregnant.

lifeEvents.title: Sees his kingdom's end written on his wall
lifeEvents.description: Throws a feast with the temple's sacred vessels and is killed that same night.

lifeEvents.title: Notices Ruth gleaning
lifeEvents.description: He has already heard what she did for Naomi, and tells his workers to leave extra grain for her on purpose.

lifeEvents.title: Praises her loyalty
lifeEvents.description: "May Yahweh repay your work... under whose wings you have come to take refuge."

lifeEvents.title: Agrees to redeem her, if the nearer kinsman won't
lifeEvents.description: He tells her to stay until morning, and names the one relative with a prior claim.

lifeEvents.title: Redeems the field and Ruth at the gate
lifeEvents.description: The nearer kinsman declines; Boaz redeems Elimelech's inheritance and takes Ruth as his wife.

lifeEvents.title: Fathers Obed
lifeEvents.description: His son with Ruth becomes the grandfather of Jesse, the father of David.

lifeEvents.title: Condemns Jesus for blasphemy
lifeEvents.description: Tears his robes and declares Jesus's claim to be the Son of Man blasphemy.

lifeEvents.title: His offering is not accepted
lifeEvents.description: He brings fruit of the ground; God has no regard for it, and Cain's face falls.

lifeEvents.title: Warned that sin crouches at the door
lifeEvents.description: God tells him sin's desire is for him, but he is to rule over it.

lifeEvents.title: Kills his brother
lifeEvents.description: He speaks to Abel in the field, and there he murders him.

lifeEvents.title: Marked and sent east
lifeEvents.description: Made a wanderer, but given a mark so no one who finds him will kill him.

lifeEvents.title: Spies out Canaan
lifeEvents.description: He silences the people's fear: "Let's go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able."

lifeEvents.title: Promised he will enter the land
lifeEvents.description: "Because he had another spirit with him, and has followed me fully" — he and Joshua alone of their generation will enter Canaan.

lifeEvents.title: Receives Hebron at eighty-five
lifeEvents.description: He asks Joshua to keep the promise Moses made forty-five years earlier, and is given the hill country of the Anakim.

lifeEvents.title: Walks with the risen Jesus without recognizing him
lifeEvents.description: Recognizes Jesus only when he breaks bread at the table in Emmaus.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes one of the first Gentile converts
lifeEvents.description: Is told in a vision to send for Peter, then receives the Holy Spirit and baptism.

lifeEvents.title: Proclaims the return from exile
lifeEvents.description: Declares that Yahweh has charged him to rebuild the temple, and any of God's people may go up to Jerusalem.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses to defile himself with the king's food
lifeEvents.description: Asks to be tested on vegetables and water instead of the king's rich food and wine.

lifeEvents.title: Interprets Nebuchadnezzar's dream and is promoted
lifeEvents.description: Reveals the king's dream and its meaning after praying with his three friends.

lifeEvents.title: Reads the writing on Belshazzar's wall
lifeEvents.description: Interprets the handwriting announcing the end of Belshazzar's kingdom.

lifeEvents.title: Survives a night in the lions' den
lifeEvents.description: Is thrown to the lions for praying and found unharmed at dawn.

lifeEvents.title: Is tricked into sentencing Daniel to the lions
lifeEvents.description: Signs a decree forbidding prayer to anyone but himself and is forced to enforce it against Daniel.

lifeEvents.title: Anointed while still a shepherd
lifeEvents.description: Samuel anoints him in the middle of his brothers, and Yahweh's Spirit comes on him from that day.

lifeEvents.title: Defeats Goliath
lifeEvents.description: With a sling and a stone, in the name of Yahweh of Armies.

lifeEvents.title: Makes a covenant with Jonathan
lifeEvents.description: The two swear loyalty to each other and to each other's descendants forever.

lifeEvents.title: Flees Saul's jealousy
lifeEvents.description: He dodges a thrown spear and spends years as a fugitive in the wilderness.

lifeEvents.title: Spares Saul's life twice
lifeEvents.description: With a clear chance to kill him both times, he refuses to raise a hand against Yahweh's anointed.

lifeEvents.title: Laments Saul and Jonathan
lifeEvents.description: Tears his clothes at the news and composes a lament instead of celebrating.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes king over all Israel
lifeEvents.description: Anointed at Hebron by the elders of every tribe; takes Jerusalem as his city.

lifeEvents.title: Dances before the ark
lifeEvents.description: Brings the ark to Jerusalem, dancing with all his might; his wife Michal despises him for it.

lifeEvents.title: Receives God's covenant
lifeEvents.description: Wants to build God a house; is promised instead that God will build his house — a throne established forever.

lifeEvents.title: Shows kindness to Mephibosheth
lifeEvents.description: Restores Saul's land to Jonathan's crippled son and gives him a permanent place at the king's table.

lifeEvents.title: Takes Bathsheba and has Uriah killed
lifeEvents.description: Sends for another man's wife, then arranges her husband's death in battle to cover it up.

lifeEvents.title: Confronted and confesses
lifeEvents.description: "You are the man." David says, "I have sinned against Yahweh."

lifeEvents.title: Flees Jerusalem before Absalom
lifeEvents.description: Chooses to leave his own city rather than fight his son within it.

lifeEvents.title: Mourns Absalom's death
lifeEvents.description: "O Absalom, my son, my son!" — grief that overshadows the victory over the rebellion.

lifeEvents.title: Buys the threshing floor for the temple
lifeEvents.description: After the census and the plague, refuses to give God an offering that costs him nothing, and names the site the house of God.

lifeEvents.title: Prepares for the temple and charges Solomon
lifeEvents.description: Gathers materials on a vast scale and tells his son to be strong and build the sanctuary.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses Yahweh before the assembly
lifeEvents.description: "All things come from you, and of your own we have given you."

lifeEvents.title: Judges Israel and summons Barak
lifeEvents.description: She calls Barak to battle and agrees to go with him when he won't go alone.

lifeEvents.title: Sings the victory song
lifeEvents.description: "The rulers ceased in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose."

lifeEvents.title: Paid to betray Samson
lifeEvents.description: Philistine rulers offer her silver to find the secret of his strength.

lifeEvents.title: Discovers his secret
lifeEvents.description: She wears him down with the same question until he finally tells her the truth.

lifeEvents.title: Pleads for Jeremiah's life and organizes his rescue
lifeEvents.description: Is the only official to speak up for Jeremiah, left to die in a cistern, and gets him pulled out.

lifeEvents.title: Raised up as a deliverer
lifeEvents.description: Israel cries out under Moabite oppression, and Yahweh raises up this left-handed Benjamite.

lifeEvents.title: Kills Eglon alone
lifeEvents.description: He gets the king alone with a private message and a hidden sword.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes high priest
lifeEvents.description: Moses puts Aaron's garments on him on Mount Hor, the same day Aaron dies.

lifeEvents.title: Raises Samuel at the tabernacle
lifeEvents.description: He takes in the boy Hannah gives him.

lifeEvents.title: Teaches Samuel to recognize God's voice
lifeEvents.description: After the third time, he realizes it is Yahweh calling and tells Samuel how to answer.

lifeEvents.title: Dies when he hears the ark is captured
lifeEvents.description: At ninety-eight, he falls backward off his seat and breaks his neck.

lifeEvents.title: Fed by ravens, sustains a widow
lifeEvents.description: Announces the drought, is fed at a brook, then keeps a foreign widow's household alive through the famine.

lifeEvents.title: Calls down fire on Mount Carmel
lifeEvents.description: Wins a public contest against 450 prophets of Baal.

lifeEvents.title: Meets God at Horeb
lifeEvents.description: Flees Jezebel wanting to die, and hears God in a still small voice instead of wind, earthquake, or fire.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts Ahab over Naboth
lifeEvents.description: Meets Ahab at the stolen vineyard with God's sentence on his house.

lifeEvents.title: Taken up to heaven in a whirlwind
lifeEvents.description: A chariot of fire separates him from Elisha, and he is carried up alive.

lifeEvents.title: Leads his family to Moab
lifeEvents.description: He takes his wife and two sons from Bethlehem to Moab to escape a famine.

lifeEvents.title: Dies in Moab
lifeEvents.description: He never sees his family return to Bethlehem.

lifeEvents.title: Argues that Job's suffering must be deserved
lifeEvents.description: Leads the friends' argument that Job's suffering is punishment for hidden sin.

lifeEvents.title: Is rebuked by God and asks for Job's prayer
lifeEvents.description: Is told his theology was wrong and offers sacrifice as Job prays for him.

lifeEvents.title: Receives Elijah's mantle
lifeEvents.description: Asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, and parts the Jordan with the fallen cloak.

lifeEvents.title: Multiplies a widow's oil
lifeEvents.description: Fills every borrowed container so she can pay her debt and keep her sons.

lifeEvents.title: Raises the Shunammite's son
lifeEvents.description: Promises her a son, then brings the boy back to life when he later dies.

lifeEvents.title: Heals Naaman of leprosy
lifeEvents.description: Sends him to wash seven times in the Jordan; his servant Gehazi's greed then costs Gehazi the same disease.

lifeEvents.title: Blinds an Aramean army and feeds it
lifeEvents.description: Shows his frightened servant the chariots of fire, then leads the enemy into Samaria and sends them home unharmed.

lifeEvents.title: Foretells the end of the siege of Samaria
lifeEvents.description: Says food will be cheap by the next day; it happens exactly as he said.

lifeEvents.title: Dies, and revives a man from the grave
lifeEvents.description: A body thrown into his tomb touches his bones and comes back to life.

lifeEvents.title: Conceives John in her old age
lifeEvents.description: Bears a son after decades of barrenness, as the angel promised Zacharias.

lifeEvents.title: Gives birth to John
lifeEvents.description: Insists on the name John against the expectation he'd be named for his father.

lifeEvents.title: Born first, red and hairy
lifeEvents.description: The firstborn twin, with his brother gripping his heel.

lifeEvents.title: Sells his birthright
lifeEvents.description: Famished from the field, he trades it for bread and lentil stew, and despises it.

lifeEvents.title: Finds the blessing gone
lifeEvents.description: He cries out with a great and bitter cry, and plans to kill his brother.

lifeEvents.title: Runs to embrace Jacob
lifeEvents.description: Twenty years later he meets his brother with four hundred men — and falls on his neck weeping.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes queen without revealing she is a Jew
lifeEvents.description: Is taken into the king's harem, wins his favor, and is crowned queen in Vashti's place.

lifeEvents.title: Agrees to risk her life and approach the king uninvited
lifeEvents.description: Answers Mordecai's plea with "if I perish, I perish" and calls for a three-day fast.

lifeEvents.title: Invites the king and Haman to a private banquet
lifeEvents.description: Approaches the king uninvited and, instead of stating her request, invites him and Haman to two banquets.

lifeEvents.title: Exposes Haman's plot and pleads for her people's lives
lifeEvents.description: Names Haman to the king's face as the enemy plotting to destroy her and her people.

lifeEvents.title: Receives Haman's house and secures a reversing decree
lifeEvents.description: Is given Haman's estate and pleads again for a decree letting the Jews defend themselves.

lifeEvents.title: Establishes Purim as an annual feast with Mordecai
lifeEvents.description: Writes with Mordecai to confirm Purim as a permanent yearly observance.

lifeEvents.title: Made from the man's side
lifeEvents.description: God makes the woman so the man will not be alone.

lifeEvents.title: Deceived by the serpent
lifeEvents.description: Persuaded the fruit will make her wise, she takes it and eats.

lifeEvents.title: Called the mother of all living
lifeEvents.description: Adam names her Eve, because she is the mother of all the living.

lifeEvents.title: Bears Cain, then Abel
lifeEvents.description: She bears two sons, and lives to see one kill the other.

lifeEvents.title: Sees Yahweh's glory and is made a watchman
lifeEvents.description: Is called by a vision of Yahweh's throne and made responsible to warn Israel.

lifeEvents.title: Acts out Jerusalem's siege and his wife's death as signs
lifeEvents.description: Portrays the coming siege with his own body and is forbidden to mourn his wife publicly.

lifeEvents.title: Prophesies life into a valley of dry bones
lifeEvents.description: Sees Israel's national restoration pictured as dry bones rising as a living army.

lifeEvents.title: Leads a second return, devoted to studying and teaching God's law
lifeEvents.description: Arrives in Jerusalem from Babylon with full royal backing to teach the law.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts the people's intermarriage with a public confession
lifeEvents.description: Tears his robe and prays a public prayer of confession over the people's unfaithfulness.

lifeEvents.title: Reads the law aloud to the whole assembly
lifeEvents.description: Reads the Book of the Law to the people from dawn to midday at the water gate.

lifeEvents.title: Governs the remnant of Judah and is assassinated
lifeEvents.description: Is appointed governor over Judah's ruins and assassinated within months by Ishmael son of Nethaniah.

lifeEvents.title: Takes Naaman's gift, and his leprosy
lifeEvents.description: Chases Naaman down for silver and clothes behind Elisha's back, and leaves Elisha's presence a leper.

lifeEvents.title: Called a mighty man of valor
lifeEvents.description: An angel finds him threshing wheat in hiding, and calls him the opposite of how he sees himself.

lifeEvents.title: Tests God with a fleece, twice
lifeEvents.description: He asks for dew on the fleece alone, then dry fleece with dew on the ground, before he believes.

lifeEvents.title: Defeats Midian with three hundred men
lifeEvents.description: Trumpets, torches, and broken jars rout an army too large to count.

lifeEvents.title: Challenges Israel's army
lifeEvents.description: For forty days he taunts them, and no one answers.

lifeEvents.title: Killed by a shepherd's sling
lifeEvents.description: A stone to the forehead, then his own sword.

lifeEvents.title: Is bought back and loved again after leaving
lifeEvents.description: Leaves Hosea for other lovers and is bought back by him at Yahweh's command.

lifeEvents.title: Flees into the wilderness
lifeEvents.description: Mistreated after she conceives, she runs — and is found by an angel at a spring.

lifeEvents.title: Names God "the God who sees me"
lifeEvents.description: The only person in Genesis to give God a name.

lifeEvents.title: Shown a well in the desert
lifeEvents.description: Out of water and unable to watch her son die, she weeps — and God opens her eyes.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts the exiles for neglecting the temple
lifeEvents.description: Tells the returned exiles to consider their ways and get back to building Yahweh's house.

lifeEvents.title: Plots to destroy all the Jews after Mordecai's refusal to bow
lifeEvents.description: Secures the king's permission and seal for a decree to annihilate every Jew in the empire.

lifeEvents.title: Builds a gallows for Mordecai, then is forced to honor him instead
lifeEvents.description: Has a gallows built for Mordecai, then is made to lead him through the city in royal honor.

lifeEvents.title: Is exposed by Esther and hanged on his own gallows
lifeEvents.description: Is named by Esther as the Jews' enemy and hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

lifeEvents.title: Prays for a son
lifeEvents.description: In bitterness of soul, she vows to give him back to Yahweh if he answers her.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Samuel to Eli
lifeEvents.description: As soon as he is weaned, she brings him to the tabernacle and keeps her vow.

lifeEvents.title: Sings a song of praise
lifeEvents.description: "My heart exults in Yahweh! My horn is exalted in Yahweh."

lifeEvents.title: Trusts Yahweh against Sennacherib
lifeEvents.description: Spreads the Assyrian threat before God in prayer; the angel of Yahweh strikes the camp that night.

lifeEvents.title: Given fifteen more years
lifeEvents.description: Weeps and prays when told he will die; God heals him and turns the shadow back as a sign.

lifeEvents.title: Marries Gomer as a living picture of Israel's unfaithfulness
lifeEvents.description: Marries a woman who will be unfaithful, then buys her back and loves her again.

lifeEvents.title: Confirms the book's warning to Josiah
lifeEvents.description: Says judgment is coming on Judah, but not in Josiah's day, because his heart was tender.

lifeEvents.title: Born to Abraham and Sarah
lifeEvents.description: The promised son, born when his father was a hundred.

lifeEvents.title: Carries the wood up Moriah
lifeEvents.description: He asks where the lamb is, and is told God will provide one.

lifeEvents.title: Marries Rebekah
lifeEvents.description: He brings her into his mother's tent, and is comforted after Sarah's death.

lifeEvents.title: Twins born after twenty years
lifeEvents.description: He prays for his barren wife, and Esau and Jacob are born.

lifeEvents.title: God appears to him at Beersheba
lifeEvents.description: "Don't be afraid, for I am with you" — the promise made to his father, repeated to him.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses the wrong son
lifeEvents.description: Blind and old, he gives Esau's blessing to Jacob, and trembles violently when he realises.

lifeEvents.title: Sees Yahweh's holiness and volunteers to be sent
lifeEvents.description: Is purified by a coal from the altar and answers Yahweh's call with "here I am, send me."

lifeEvents.title: Assures Hezekiah against Assyria
lifeEvents.description: Delivers God's word that Sennacherib will not enter the city.

lifeEvents.title: Tells Hezekiah he will be healed
lifeEvents.description: Cries to Yahweh, and the shadow on the sundial goes ten steps back.

lifeEvents.title: Born to Hagar
lifeEvents.description: Abram's firstborn, named before birth: God hears.

lifeEvents.title: Sent away with his mother
lifeEvents.description: God hears the boy where he is and promises to make him a great nation.

lifeEvents.title: Buries his father with Isaac
lifeEvents.description: The two sons stand together at Abraham's grave.

lifeEvents.title: Born holding Esau's heel
lifeEvents.description: The second twin, named for the grip he came out with.

lifeEvents.title: Buys the birthright
lifeEvents.description: He trades a bowl of stew for his brother's rights as firstborn.

lifeEvents.title: Steals his father's blessing
lifeEvents.description: Disguised in his brother's clothes, he lies to his blind father's face.

lifeEvents.title: Dreams of the ladder at Bethel
lifeEvents.description: Running for his life, he is met with a promise: I am with you wherever you go.

lifeEvents.title: Works fourteen years for Rachel
lifeEvents.description: Deceived into marrying Leah first, he serves seven more years for the woman he loves.

lifeEvents.title: Wrestles until daybreak
lifeEvents.description: He refuses to let go without a blessing, and walks away limping and renamed Israel.

lifeEvents.title: Meets Esau again
lifeEvents.description: Braced for revenge, he is embraced instead.

lifeEvents.title: Believes Joseph is dead
lifeEvents.description: Shown the bloodied coat, he refuses to be comforted.

lifeEvents.title: Goes down to Egypt
lifeEvents.description: Told his son is alive and ruling Egypt, he goes to see him before he dies.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses his twelve sons
lifeEvents.description: He tells each of them what they will become, and dies.

lifeEvents.title: Kills Sisera with a tent peg
lifeEvents.description: She gives the fleeing commander milk and a place to sleep, then kills him there.

lifeEvents.title: Leaves his father's boat to follow Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Is called with his brother John after the miraculous catch of fish.

lifeEvents.title: Witnesses the Transfiguration
lifeEvents.description: Is one of the three disciples who sees Jesus transfigured.

lifeEvents.title: Falls asleep in Gethsemane
lifeEvents.description: Is one of the three taken further into the garden with Jesus.

lifeEvents.title: Hides and crowns the boy king Joash
lifeEvents.description: Shelters the last heir of David's line for six years, then overthrows Athaliah.

lifeEvents.title: Guides Joash to restore the temple
lifeEvents.description: As long as he lives, Joash does what is right.

lifeEvents.title: Sends teachers of the law through Judah
lifeEvents.description: Officials, Levites, and priests carry the book of the law from town to town.

lifeEvents.title: Faces invasion with prayer and singers
lifeEvents.description: Gathers Judah to fast and pray, then sends the choir out ahead of the army.

lifeEvents.title: Anointed king to end Ahab's house
lifeEvents.description: Charged by a prophet to avenge the blood of the prophets Jezebel had killed.

lifeEvents.title: Has Jezebel thrown from her window
lifeEvents.description: Ends the house of Ahab in Jezreel.

lifeEvents.title: Vows whatever comes out of his house first
lifeEvents.description: He makes the vow before going to battle against Ammon.

lifeEvents.title: Keeps his vow
lifeEvents.description: His only child comes out to meet him first, and he does as he vowed.

lifeEvents.title: Runs out to celebrate
lifeEvents.description: With tambourines and dancing, not knowing what her father had vowed.

lifeEvents.title: Asks for two months to mourn
lifeEvents.description: She asks only to grieve with her friends in the mountains before her father keeps his vow.

lifeEvents.title: Is called as a prophet to the nations while still young
lifeEvents.description: Protests his youth but is sent with Yahweh's words put in his mouth.

lifeEvents.title: Is nearly killed for his temple sermon
lifeEvents.description: Warns Jerusalem could be destroyed like Shiloh and is seized by priests and prophets demanding his death.

lifeEvents.title: Dictates his prophecies to Baruch, twice
lifeEvents.description: Has the scroll rewritten after King Jehoiakim burns the first copy.

lifeEvents.title: Is thrown in a cistern and rescued by Ebed-Melech
lifeEvents.description: Is lowered into a muddy cistern to die and pulled out on Ebed-Melech's plea.

lifeEvents.title: Lives under Gedaliah's brief governorship
lifeEvents.description: Stays in Judah under the governor appointed over the land's remnant.

lifeEvents.title: Is forced to Egypt against Yahweh's word through him
lifeEvents.description: Warns the remnant to stay in Judah, then is taken to Egypt against his own counsel anyway.

lifeEvents.title: Leads the ten tribes away
lifeEvents.description: Becomes king over the northern tribes when they reject Rehoboam.

lifeEvents.title: Builds golden calves
lifeEvents.description: Sets up rival worship at Dan and Bethel to keep Israel from returning to Jerusalem.

lifeEvents.title: Builds the altar and leads the priests home
lifeEvents.description: Returns from exile and rebuilds the altar of burnt offering alongside Zerubbabel.

lifeEvents.title: Sees the temple finished
lifeEvents.description: Leads the priests and Levites through the temple's completion and dedication.

lifeEvents.title: Is born in Bethlehem
lifeEvents.description: Is born to Mary during a Roman census and laid in a feeding trough.

lifeEvents.title: Is presented at the temple and recognized by Simeon and Anna
lifeEvents.description: Is blessed by Simeon, who calls him God's salvation for all peoples.

lifeEvents.title: Is worshiped by wise men and flees to Egypt as a child
lifeEvents.description: Receives gold, frankincense, and myrrh, then escapes Herod's slaughter of the infants.

lifeEvents.title: Is found teaching in the temple at twelve
lifeEvents.description: Amazes the teachers with his understanding and calls the temple "my Father's house."

lifeEvents.title: Is baptized by John and affirmed by the Father
lifeEvents.description: Is baptized in the Jordan; the Spirit descends and a voice from heaven affirms him.

lifeEvents.title: Resists three temptations in the wilderness
lifeEvents.description: Fasts forty days and answers the devil's three temptations with Scripture.

lifeEvents.title: Gathers his first disciples near the Jordan
lifeEvents.description: Is followed by Andrew and Peter, then calls Philip, who brings Nathanael.

lifeEvents.title: Turns water to wine at a wedding in Cana
lifeEvents.description: Performs his first sign, revealing his glory to his new disciples.

lifeEvents.title: Calls Peter, Andrew, James, and John to full-time discipleship
lifeEvents.description: Gives Simon a miraculous catch of fish, then calls the four fishermen to leave everything and follow him.

lifeEvents.title: Teaches the Sermon on the Mount
lifeEvents.description: Delivers the Beatitudes and his core teaching on the law, prayer, worry, and judgment.

lifeEvents.title: Teaches the parable of the sower
lifeEvents.description: Explains why he teaches in parables and what the different soils represent.

lifeEvents.title: Tells the parable of the good Samaritan
lifeEvents.description: Answers "who is my neighbor?" with a story about a despised outsider showing real mercy.

lifeEvents.title: Tells the parable of the prodigal son
lifeEvents.description: Pictures God's welcome for the repentant and his appeal to the resentful obedient son.

lifeEvents.title: Calms a storm with a word
lifeEvents.description: Rebukes the wind and sea while crossing the lake by boat.

lifeEvents.title: Feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish
lifeEvents.description: Multiplies a small meal to feed a huge crowd, with baskets of leftovers.

lifeEvents.title: Walks on water and rescues Peter
lifeEvents.description: Comes to the disciples' boat walking on the sea and catches Peter as he sinks.

lifeEvents.title: Receives Peter's confession and predicts his death
lifeEvents.description: Is confessed as the Christ, then foretells his suffering, death, and resurrection for the first time.

lifeEvents.title: Is transfigured before Peter, James, and John
lifeEvents.description: Shines with glory alongside Moses and Elijah while the Father speaks from a cloud.

lifeEvents.title: Teaches Nicodemus about being born again
lifeEvents.description: Explains the new birth and God's love for the world to a Pharisee who comes to him at night.

lifeEvents.title: Reveals himself as the Messiah to a Samaritan woman
lifeEvents.description: Offers living water and tells a Samaritan woman plainly that he is the Christ.

lifeEvents.title: Raises Lazarus from the dead
lifeEvents.description: Weeps at Lazarus's tomb, then calls him back to life after four days.

lifeEvents.title: Invites himself to Zacchaeus's house
lifeEvents.description: Calls a despised tax collector down from a tree and brings salvation to his house.

lifeEvents.title: Tells a wealthy man to sell everything and follow him
lifeEvents.description: Watches a rich young man walk away sad rather than give up his possessions.

lifeEvents.title: Enters Jerusalem on a donkey to shouts of Hosanna
lifeEvents.description: Fulfills Zechariah's prophecy of a humble king entering the city.

lifeEvents.title: Shares a final Passover meal and institutes communion
lifeEvents.description: Foretells his betrayal and gives the bread and cup new meaning.

lifeEvents.title: Washes his disciples' feet
lifeEvents.description: Models servant leadership and gives a new commandment to love one another.

lifeEvents.title: Comforts his disciples before his death
lifeEvents.description: Promises peace, describes himself as the way and the vine, and warns of trouble ahead.

lifeEvents.title: Prays in Gethsemane before his arrest
lifeEvents.description: Asks three times that the coming suffering might pass, then submits to it.

lifeEvents.title: Is betrayed with a kiss and arrested
lifeEvents.description: Is identified by Judas and taken without resistance.

lifeEvents.title: Is condemned by the council for claiming to be the Christ
lifeEvents.description: Answers Caiaphas's demand plainly and is condemned for blasphemy.

lifeEvents.title: Is condemned by Pilate and handed over to be crucified
lifeEvents.description: Is chosen for death over Barabbas and flogged before crucifixion.

lifeEvents.title: Is crucified and dies
lifeEvents.description: Is mocked, crucified between two criminals, and dies after forgiving his executioners.

lifeEvents.title: Is buried in Joseph of Arimathea's tomb
lifeEvents.description: Is wrapped and laid in a new tomb, which is then sealed and guarded.

lifeEvents.title: Rises from the dead
lifeEvents.description: Is found alive by the women at the tomb, exactly as he had said.

lifeEvents.title: Appears first to Mary Magdalene
lifeEvents.description: Reveals himself by speaking her name outside the empty tomb.

lifeEvents.title: Walks unrecognized with two disciples to Emmaus
lifeEvents.description: Explains the Scriptures concerning himself, then is recognized in the breaking of bread.

lifeEvents.title: Shows Thomas his wounds
lifeEvents.description: Invites doubting Thomas to touch his hands and side.

lifeEvents.title: Sends the disciples to make disciples of all nations
lifeEvents.description: Claims all authority and commissions the eleven before his ascension.

lifeEvents.title: Ascends to heaven
lifeEvents.description: Blesses the disciples at Bethany and is carried up into heaven.

lifeEvents.title: Has Naboth falsely accused and killed
lifeEvents.description: Arranges false witnesses so Naboth is stoned and Ahab can take his vineyard.

lifeEvents.title: Thrown from a window at Jehu's command
lifeEvents.description: The dogs leave only her skull, feet, and hands, exactly as Elijah had foretold.

lifeEvents.title: Carries out David's order against Uriah
lifeEvents.description: Places Uriah where the fighting is fiercest, at David's instruction, so he'll be killed.

lifeEvents.title: Kills Absalom
lifeEvents.description: Against David's express order to deal gently with him, thrusts three darts through Absalom's heart.

lifeEvents.title: Hidden and crowned as a boy
lifeEvents.description: Kept safe in the temple by the priest Jehoiada through Athaliah's purge, and made king at seven.

lifeEvents.title: Restores the temple
lifeEvents.description: Does right for as long as Jehoiada the priest is alive to guide him.

lifeEvents.title: Has Zechariah stoned in the temple court
lifeEvents.description: After Jehoiada dies, turns to idols and kills the priest's son for rebuking him.

lifeEvents.title: Loses everything but refuses to curse God
lifeEvents.description: Loses his children, wealth, and health in a single day and refuses to curse God.

lifeEvents.title: Laments his suffering and rejects his friends' theology
lifeEvents.description: Argues his innocence against his friends' insistence that his suffering is deserved.

lifeEvents.title: Is answered by Yahweh out of the whirlwind and repents
lifeEvents.description: Sees God's power displayed in creation and repents in dust and ashes.

lifeEvents.title: Is restored with double what he had before
lifeEvents.description: Receives double his former wealth, ten more children, and a long life.

lifeEvents.title: Hides her son three months
lifeEvents.description: Seeing he is a fine child, she conceals him from Pharaoh's decree as long as she can.

lifeEvents.title: Sets him afloat in a basket
lifeEvents.description: She coats a papyrus basket with tar and pitch and lays it among the reeds by the riverbank.

lifeEvents.title: Hired to nurse her own son
lifeEvents.description: Pharaoh's daughter unknowingly pays Moses' own mother to nurse him.

lifeEvents.title: Leaves his father's boat to follow Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Is called with his brother James after the miraculous catch of fish.

lifeEvents.title: Witnesses the Transfiguration
lifeEvents.description: Is one of the three disciples who sees Jesus transfigured.

lifeEvents.title: Falls asleep in Gethsemane
lifeEvents.description: Is one of the three taken further into the garden with Jesus.

lifeEvents.title: Is entrusted with the care of Jesus's mother
lifeEvents.description: Takes Mary into his own home at Jesus's request from the cross.

lifeEvents.title: Is present when Peter heals a lame man
lifeEvents.description: Accompanies Peter to the temple and witnesses the healing.

lifeEvents.title: Exiled on Patmos, receives the Revelation
lifeEvents.description: Exiled on Patmos, receives and writes down the Revelation of Jesus Christ.

lifeEvents.title: Is born to Zacharias and Elizabeth
lifeEvents.description: Is born and named John, exactly as the angel Gabriel instructed.

lifeEvents.title: Preaches repentance and baptizes in the Jordan
lifeEvents.description: Calls Israel to repent and points ahead to the one coming after him.

lifeEvents.title: Baptizes Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Objects, then baptizes Jesus and witnesses the Spirit descend on him.

lifeEvents.title: Points his own disciples toward Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Calls Jesus "the Lamb of God," prompting Andrew to follow him.

lifeEvents.title: Flees Nineveh and is swallowed by a fish
lifeEvents.description: Boards a ship away from his call, is thrown overboard in a storm, and prays from inside a great fish.

lifeEvents.title: Preaches to Nineveh and resents its repentance
lifeEvents.description: Sees the whole city repent and is angry that Yahweh spares it.

lifeEvents.title: Makes a covenant with David
lifeEvents.description: "The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul."

lifeEvents.title: Warns David of his father's intent
lifeEvents.description: He chooses the friendship over his own claim to the throne.

lifeEvents.title: Dies at Gilboa
lifeEvents.description: Killed alongside his father and brothers in the battle against the Philistines.

lifeEvents.title: Dreams that his brothers bow
lifeEvents.description: The favourite son tells them, and they hate him all the more.

lifeEvents.title: Thrown in a pit and sold
lifeEvents.description: His brothers strip him, pit him, and sell him to traders for twenty pieces of silver.

lifeEvents.title: Prospers in Potiphar's house
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh is with him, and everything he does succeeds.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses Potiphar's wife
lifeEvents.description: "How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?" — and he is imprisoned for it.

lifeEvents.title: Forgotten in prison for two years
lifeEvents.description: He interprets the cupbearer's dream and asks to be remembered. He isn't.

lifeEvents.title: Reads Pharaoh's dream
lifeEvents.description: Seven years of plenty, seven of famine — and a plan to survive them.

lifeEvents.title: Made second in Egypt
lifeEvents.description: Pharaoh sets him over the whole land, with the signet ring off his own hand.

lifeEvents.title: Reveals himself to his brothers
lifeEvents.description: He weeps so loudly the Egyptians hear it: I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?

lifeEvents.title: Sees his father again
lifeEvents.description: He falls on Jacob's neck in Goshen and weeps a long time.

lifeEvents.title: Forgives his brothers outright
lifeEvents.description: "You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive."

lifeEvents.title: Is told in a dream to take Mary as his wife
lifeEvents.description: Learns Mary's pregnancy is from the Holy Spirit and names the child Jesus.

lifeEvents.title: Travels to Bethlehem for the census
lifeEvents.description: Brings Mary to his ancestral city, where Jesus is born.

lifeEvents.title: Presents Jesus at the temple
lifeEvents.description: Marvels at Simeon's and Anna's recognition of the child.

lifeEvents.title: Flees to Egypt, then settles in Nazareth
lifeEvents.description: Follows repeated dream-warnings to protect Jesus, ending in Nazareth.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Jesus his own tomb
lifeEvents.description: Asks Pilate for the body and buries it in his own new tomb.

lifeEvents.title: Defeats Amalek
lifeEvents.description: He leads Israel's fighting men while Moses' upheld hands decide the battle.

lifeEvents.title: Won't leave the Tent of Meeting
lifeEvents.description: After Moses speaks with God face to face and leaves the tent, his young aide stays behind.

lifeEvents.title: Spies out Canaan
lifeEvents.description: One of the twelve, and one of only two who came back believing Israel could take the land.

lifeEvents.title: Commissioned by Moses
lifeEvents.description: Moses lays hands on him before all Israel; he is filled with the spirit of wisdom.

lifeEvents.title: Takes charge after Moses
lifeEvents.description: God tells him directly to be strong and courageous, and that he will be with him just as he was with Moses.

lifeEvents.title: Sends spies into Jericho
lifeEvents.description: They are hidden by a woman named Rahab and return with word that the city is already afraid.

lifeEvents.title: Leads Israel across the Jordan
lifeEvents.description: The river stops flowing the moment the priests carrying the ark step into it.

lifeEvents.title: Takes Jericho
lifeEvents.description: Seven days of marching, then a shout, and the wall falls.

lifeEvents.title: Uncovers Achan's sin
lifeEvents.description: After defeat at Ai, he finds and deals with the hidden plunder that caused it.

lifeEvents.title: Deceived by the Gibeonites
lifeEvents.description: He makes a treaty with them without asking God first, believing their disguise.

lifeEvents.title: Asks the sun to stand still
lifeEvents.description: In front of all Israel, he asks Yahweh to stop the sun and moon so the battle can be finished.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Caleb Hebron
lifeEvents.description: He honors the forty-five-year-old promise and gives Caleb the hill country he asked for.

lifeEvents.title: Gathers Israel to choose
lifeEvents.description: "As for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh."

lifeEvents.title: Hears the lost Book of the Law
lifeEvents.description: Tears his clothes when he realizes how far Judah has fallen from it.

lifeEvents.title: Renews the covenant and purges idolatry
lifeEvents.description: Reads the law to the whole nation and tears down every high place and idol in the land.

lifeEvents.title: Betrays Jesus with a kiss
lifeEvents.description: Leads an armed crowd to Jesus and identifies him with a prearranged signal.

lifeEvents.title: Returns the silver and hangs himself
lifeEvents.description: Confesses his sin to the unmoved chief priests and takes his own life.

lifeEvents.title: Leads a rebellion against Moses and Aaron
lifeEvents.description: He gathers two hundred fifty leaders and accuses them of taking too much on themselves.

lifeEvents.title: Swallowed by the earth
lifeEvents.description: The ground opens beneath him, his household, and everything he owns.

lifeEvents.title: Dies and is raised by Jesus after four days
lifeEvents.description: Is called out of the tomb still wrapped in graveclothes.

lifeEvents.title: Given to Jacob in Rachel's place
lifeEvents.description: Veiled and substituted by her father, she wakes married to a man who wanted her sister.

lifeEvents.title: Bears son after son
lifeEvents.description: Seeing she is unloved, God opens her womb; she names her sons for her longing to be loved.

lifeEvents.title: Names her fourth son Judah
lifeEvents.description: "This time I will praise Yahweh" — the line the kings will come from.

lifeEvents.title: Chooses the Jordan valley
lifeEvents.description: Given first pick, he takes the well-watered plain and pitches his tent toward Sodom.

lifeEvents.title: Rescued by Abram
lifeEvents.description: Captured when the kings sack Sodom, he is brought back by his uncle's night raid.

lifeEvents.title: Pulled out of Sodom
lifeEvents.description: The angels seize his hand and lead him out; his wife looks back.

lifeEvents.title: Leads Judah into deep idolatry
lifeEvents.description: Builds altars to other gods inside Yahweh's own temple.

lifeEvents.title: Humbles himself in Babylon and is restored
lifeEvents.description: Prays in captivity, is brought back to Jerusalem, and spends his last years removing the idols he had built.

lifeEvents.title: Confesses Jesus as the Christ despite her grief
lifeEvents.description: Meets Jesus on the road grieving her brother, but still confesses him as the Son of God.

lifeEvents.title: Is told by Gabriel she will bear the Messiah
lifeEvents.description: Answers "let it be done to me" and visits Elizabeth, who recognizes her unborn son.

lifeEvents.title: Gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem
lifeEvents.description: Gives birth away from home during a Roman census and is visited by shepherds.

lifeEvents.title: Is warned by Simeon that a sword will pierce her soul
lifeEvents.description: Presents Jesus at the temple and hears Simeon's blessing and warning.

lifeEvents.title: Flees to Egypt with Joseph and Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Escapes Herod's slaughter of the infants in Bethlehem.

lifeEvents.title: Searches three days for the missing boy Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Finds him in the temple among the teachers.

lifeEvents.title: Watches her son die and is entrusted to John
lifeEvents.description: Is present at the cross and given into John's care by Jesus.

lifeEvents.title: Watches the crucifixion and burial
lifeEvents.description: Stays near Jesus through his death and sees where he is buried.

lifeEvents.title: Watches where Jesus is buried
lifeEvents.description: Sits opposite the tomb with another Mary after Joseph seals it.

lifeEvents.title: Finds the tomb empty and tells the disciples
lifeEvents.description: Discovers the stone rolled away and is met by Jesus himself.

lifeEvents.title: Is the first to see the risen Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Recognizes Jesus when he speaks her name and carries the news to the disciples.

lifeEvents.title: Falls at Jesus's feet weeping for Lazarus
lifeEvents.description: Grieves her brother's death and moves Jesus to tears.

lifeEvents.title: Is called from his tax booth to follow Jesus
lifeEvents.description: Follows Jesus immediately and hosts a feast for tax collectors and sinners.

lifeEvents.title: Is chosen by lot to replace Judas
lifeEvents.description: Is selected over Joseph Barsabbas to complete the twelve apostles.

lifeEvents.title: Shown kindness by David
lifeEvents.description: Crippled in both feet since childhood, is given his grandfather Saul's land and a permanent seat at the king's table.

lifeEvents.title: Joins Daniel's food test
lifeEvents.description: Is renamed and trained for the king's service alongside Daniel.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses to bow and walks out of the furnace unharmed
lifeEvents.description: Refuses to worship Nebuchadnezzar's image and survives the furnace.

lifeEvents.title: Despises David's worship
lifeEvents.description: Watches him dance before the ark and mocks him for it when he returns home.

lifeEvents.title: Watches over the basket
lifeEvents.description: She stands at a distance to see what will happen to her brother.

lifeEvents.title: Arranges for their mother to nurse him
lifeEvents.description: She steps forward and offers to find a Hebrew nurse for the child - their own mother.

lifeEvents.title: Leads the women in song
lifeEvents.description: She takes a tambourine and leads the women in singing and dancing after the sea closes over Egypt's army.

lifeEvents.title: Speaks against Moses
lifeEvents.description: She and Aaron challenge Moses over his marriage and his unique standing before God.

lifeEvents.title: Struck with leprosy
lifeEvents.description: She is shut outside the camp seven days after Moses prays for her.

lifeEvents.title: Dies at Kadesh
lifeEvents.description: The text records her death and burial in a single sentence.

lifeEvents.title: Raises Esther and uncovers a plot against the king
lifeEvents.description: Raises his orphaned cousin as his own daughter, then reports an assassination plot through her.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses to bow to Haman, provoking his plot against the Jews
lifeEvents.description: Will not bow to the newly promoted Haman, who turns his wrath on all the Jews as a result.

lifeEvents.title: Urges Esther to intercede for her people
lifeEvents.description: Presses Esther that she may have come to her position "for such a time as this."

lifeEvents.title: Is honored by the king the night Haman planned to hang him
lifeEvents.description: Is led through the city in royal honor by Haman himself, the same night Haman built a gallows for him.

lifeEvents.title: Is promoted to Haman's former position
lifeEvents.description: Is set over Haman's house and given his signet ring.

lifeEvents.title: Establishes Purim and becomes second only to the king
lifeEvents.description: Rises to be next to King Ahasuerus, seeking the good of his people.

lifeEvents.title: Hidden three months, then set adrift
lifeEvents.description: His mother hides him as long as she can, then sets him afloat on the Nile in a coated basket.

lifeEvents.title: Found and adopted by Pharaoh's daughter
lifeEvents.description: She recognises him as a Hebrew child, has compassion on him, and raises him as her own son.

lifeEvents.title: Kills an Egyptian, and flees
lifeEvents.description: Grown and aware of his people's suffering, he kills an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, and flees when it becomes known.

lifeEvents.title: Meets Zipporah at a well
lifeEvents.description: He defends a priest's seven daughters from shepherds driving them off, and is given one of them in marriage.

lifeEvents.title: Sees the burning bush
lifeEvents.description: A bush burns and is not consumed. God calls his name twice; he answers, Here I am.

lifeEvents.title: Called and sent to confront Pharaoh
lifeEvents.description: Told to bring Israel out of Egypt, he objects four times - who am I, what is your name, what if they don't believe, I am slow of speech - and is answered every time.

lifeEvents.title: Returns to Egypt
lifeEvents.description: He takes his wife and sons, puts them on a donkey, and sets out with God's staff in his hand.

lifeEvents.title: Reunited with Aaron
lifeEvents.description: Aaron meets him at God's mountain and kisses him; together they persuade Israel's elders.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts Pharaoh again and again
lifeEvents.description: He and Aaron repeat the same demand through nine plagues, and Pharaoh's heart hardens every time.

lifeEvents.title: Institutes the Passover
lifeEvents.description: He tells Israel to mark their doors with blood on the night of the tenth plague.

lifeEvents.title: Leads Israel through the sea
lifeEvents.description: He stretches out his hand and the sea divides; Israel crosses on dry ground.

lifeEvents.title: Sings on the far shore
lifeEvents.description: "Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation."

lifeEvents.title: Brings bread and water from nothing
lifeEvents.description: He relays God's provision of manna and strikes the rock at Horeb for water.

lifeEvents.title: Receives the covenant and the commandments
lifeEvents.description: God offers Israel a covenant through him, and gives the Ten Commandments.

lifeEvents.title: Breaks the tablets, then intercedes
lifeEvents.description: Furious at the golden calf, he shatters the tablets — then goes back up the mountain and offers to be blotted out himself rather than let the people be destroyed.

lifeEvents.title: Hears God proclaim his own character
lifeEvents.description: "Merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth."

lifeEvents.title: Can't enter his own tent
lifeEvents.description: God's glory fills the finished tabernacle so completely that even Moses is kept out.

lifeEvents.title: Ordains Aaron and his sons
lifeEvents.description: He carries out seven days of ordination rites exactly as commanded.

lifeEvents.title: Rules on the blasphemer
lifeEvents.description: He holds the man until Yahweh tells him exactly what the community must do.

lifeEvents.title: Prays for Miriam's healing
lifeEvents.description: The instant she is struck with leprosy, he cries out, "Heal her, God, I beg you!"

lifeEvents.title: Sends twelve spies into Canaan
lifeEvents.description: Ten come back afraid; only Caleb and Joshua say Israel can take the land.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts Korah's rebellion
lifeEvents.description: He tells the assembly the ground itself will show who Yahweh sent.

lifeEvents.title: Strikes the rock in anger
lifeEvents.description: Told to speak to the rock, he strikes it twice instead — and is barred from entering the promised land for it.

lifeEvents.title: Buries Aaron on Mount Hor
lifeEvents.description: He strips Aaron of his priestly garments and puts them on Eleazar before Aaron dies.

lifeEvents.title: Makes the bronze serpent
lifeEvents.description: Anyone bitten by the venomous snakes who looks at it lives.

lifeEvents.title: Commissions Joshua as his successor
lifeEvents.description: He lays his hands on Joshua in front of all Israel and tells him to be strong and courageous.
